taiwan|ongoing|kinmen and pratas|maritim.text: 2–7 Nov — Kinmen and Pratas: The CGA recorded CCG ships in Kinmen restricted waters on 2, 4 and 6 Nov, and a CCG vessel operated near the Pratas Islands on 7 Nov. On 3 Nov the research vessel Haiyang Dizhi 8 and four Chinese fishing boats were spotted near Kaohsiung port.

taiwan|2026-11-06|taipei|other.text: 6–7 Nov — Taipei: The TAIEX fell 1,873 points on 6 Nov amid the PLA surge, and the government activated its NT$500 billion National Stabilization Fund on 7 Nov.

philippines|2026-11-03|scarborough bajo.text: 3 Nov — Scarborough (Bajo de Masinloc) Shoal: The PCG said it was still assessing a Chinese vessel carrying unidentified sensor-fitted equipment inside the lagoon, whose bow and IMO numbers match no known research ship. The CCG announced 'law-enforcement patrols' at the shoal the same day.

philippines|2026-11-08|mamasapano maguin.text: 8 Nov — Mamasapano, Maguindanao del Sur: Unidentified gunmen ambushed and killed three people, including two CAFGU active auxiliaries (Philstar).

philippines|2026-11-08|mindanao|armed-at.text: 8 Nov — Mindanao: Three soldiers were wounded in crossfire while trying to stop a clash between the Labao and Gaosil Maranao clans (Philstar).

philippines|2026-11-04|subic bay|militar.text: 4 Nov — Subic Bay: The US delivered T38 Devil Ray unmanned surface vessels to the Philippine Marines amid continued Chinese pressure in the South China Sea.

south korea|2026-11-04|east sea|missile-.text: 4 Nov — East Sea: The JCS detected multiple North Korean missiles launched from Sondok, South Hamgyong, the North's fourth weapons launch in a month and its 11th suspected ballistic launch of 2026, ahead of combined ROK–US drills.

south korea|ongoing|inter korean border|.text: 1–2 Nov — Inter-Korean border: The ROK military said it had not confirmed any operation of North Korean loudspeakers aimed at the South despite Kim Yo Jong's October deadline. North Korean MDL crossings during fortification work continue to draw warning broadcasts and warning shots, mostly on the eastern front.

south korea|2026-11-10|seoul dmz|politic.text: 10 Nov — Seoul / DMZ: Kim Yo Jong rejected the UN Secretary-General's call for dialogue and called Seoul's findings on the 21 Sep DMZ mine blast, which wounded three ROK officers, fabricated. A joint ROK–UNC investigation attributed the blast to North Korean mines.

vietnam|2026-11-09|hanoi|diplomatic.text: 9 Nov — Hanoi: Vietnam and Australia held their defence policy dialogue, part of Hanoi's continued defence hedging after Indian NSA Ajit Doval's 2 Nov visit agreed co-production and maritime information-sharing.

vietnam|ongoing|ban keun laos|military-a.text: Early Nov — Ban Keun, Laos (Vietnam's western flank): A Vietnamese official told AP that a Chinese deployment to the new Ban Keun airfield in Laos would 'naturally place a certain degree of additional military pressure on Vietnam'.

vietnam|ongoing|vietnam china border|dip.text: 10–11 Nov — Vietnam–China border: Hanoi and Beijing agreed to strengthen coordination on border management and protection. No Vietnam–China maritime incident was found for 5–12 Nov.

japan|2026-11-09|senkaku islands near ku.text: 9 Nov — Senkaku Islands (near Kuba Island): Four China Coast Guard ships entered Japanese territorial waters and left about two hours later, the first such entry since 10 Oct (Jiji via Nippon.com).

japan|2026-11-01|miyako strait|military-.text: 1 Nov — Miyako Strait: According to the Joint Staff, a Chinese destroyer and a fast combat support ship transited into the Pacific, and the destroyer later returned to the East China Sea.

japan|2026-11-02|okinawa miyako gap|mili.text: 2 Nov — Okinawa–Miyako gap: The ASDF scrambled fighters against Chinese WZ-7 high-altitude reconnaissance drones flying from the East China Sea into the Pacific and back.

japan|ongoing|western pacific|military-a.text: 3–10 Nov — Western Pacific: More than 100 Chinese naval and coast guard ships, including the Liaoning carrier group, were deployed in clusters between Taiwan and Guam, which Taiwan calls 'area denial' drills against outside intervention.

indonesia|2026-11-08|camp biru dekai dis.text: 8 Nov — Camp Biru, Kali Senami, Dekai District, Yahukimo, Highland Papua: TNI troops (Satgas Rajawali V and Marines) fought a TPNPB-OPM group led by Kopitua Heluka, pushed back about 15 fighters and took their camp, seizing seven firearms. No casualties were reported.

indonesia|2026-11-08|papua|other.text: 8 Nov (report) — Papua: The Operation Damai Cartenz 2026 task force said it had arrested a suspect in the shooting death of police officer Brigpol Ronald Enok and seized seven firearms from armed groups (Metro TV).

indonesia|2026-10-29|maybrat southwest p.text: 29 Oct — Maybrat, Southwest Papua: Marines detained three alleged TPNPB-OPM members whom the military links to attacks on security posts and Trans-Bintuni road workers.

thailand|2026-11-09|ban kampong baru mae.place: Ban Kampong Baru, Mae Wat, Than To district, Yala
thailand|2026-11-09|ban kampong baru mae.text: 9 Nov — Ban Kampong Baru, Mae Wat, Than To district, Yala: Security forces killed alleged insurgent trainer Sa-udi Ting-useng, wanted over the 2019 Lam Phaya attack that killed 15, in a dawn gunfight about 1 km from the Malaysian border during a three-day operation. Other suspects escaped.

thailand|2026-11-07|maha wan subdistrict.place: Maha Wan subdistrict, Mae Sot, Tak
thailand|2026-11-07|maha wan subdistrict.text: 7 Nov — Maha Wan subdistrict, Mae Sot, Tak: Artillery shells from fighting between Myanmar junta troops and resistance forces in Myawaddy Township landed in Thailand, damaging several houses without injuries.

bangladesh|2026-11-03|joydebpur gazipur|.text: 3 Nov — Joydebpur, Gazipur: Garment worker Toufiq Hossain died of injuries sustained in a clash during the minimum-wage protests, HRW said, the first confirmed death of the unrest. HRW reported police using batons and tear gas against thousands of workers.

bangladesh|2026-11-12|mouchak kaliakair.text: 12 Nov — Mouchak, Kaliakair, Gazipur: Workers blocked the Dhaka–Tangail highway for about three hours. Police fired sound grenades to clear it, and seven factories in the area declared a holiday (Prothom Alo).

bangladesh|ongoing|gazipur|unrest.text: Early Nov — Gazipur: Two garment factories were shut indefinitely after workers vandalised their premises, as protests for a Tk 30,000 minimum wage continued across Savar, Ashulia, Gazipur and Narayanganj.

sri lanka|2026-11-02|kappalthurai uppuve.text: 2 Nov — Kappalthurai, Uppuveli, Trincomalee: A gunman with a suspected T-56 rifle fired on a hired three-wheeler, killing one man (identified by police as a Navy serviceman) and wounding two. Police suspect a drug-trafficking dispute.

sri lanka|2026-11-06|dikwella matara|oth.text: 6 Nov — Dikwella, Matara: Police arrested the suspected gunman in the Trincomalee shooting, a former army soldier who had been formally discharged.

venezuela|2026-10-30|apure state|airstri.text: 30 Oct (reported 5–10 Nov) — Apure state: Venezuelan armed forces struck an ELN camp and cocaine site near the Colombian border, with US drones and intelligence according to The New York Times and with Colombian-supplied coordinates according to Cambio. Reported deaths range from about nine (La Silla Vacia) to 23 (FundaRedes); Caracas has not commented publicly.

venezuela|2026-11-06|el rodeo i prison m.text: 6 Nov — El Rodeo I prison, Miranda: Maria Corina Machado visited relatives of political prisoners camped outside the prison and demanded the release of all of them. Foro Penal counts 322 political prisoners still held.

venezuela|2026-11-08|caracas|political.text: 8 Nov — Caracas: Opposition negotiator Dinorah Figuera said the government will soon release a new group of political prisoners ahead of a fourth round of talks. The families dismantled the protest camp at El Rodeo I after about 10 months, and US Secretary of State Rubio urged foreign minister Oliver Blanco to continue the releases.

colombia|2026-11-07|santa rosa del sur b.text: 7 Nov — Santa Rosa del Sur, Bolivar: Explosive drones struck an army post, killing three soldiers and wounding at least 16, according to the military. Local reports put the toll higher. The ELN and the Clan del Golfo operate in the area; no group has been formally named.

colombia|2026-11-09|tibu norte de santan.text: 9 Nov — Tibu, Norte de Santander (Catatumbo): The government's seventh bombing ('Operation Noah') hit a camp of FARC dissident Front 33. Four alleged members were killed and six captured, including a commission leader close to 'Andrey Avendano', with US MQ-9 surveillance support.

colombia|2026-11-10|undisclosed location.text: 10 Nov — Undisclosed location: President De la Espriella announced an eighth air strike, at 22:17, against an unnamed 'narcoterrorist structure'. No location or casualties have been released yet.

colombia|ongoing|choco|ground-clash.text: 9 Nov — Choco: Fighting between the Clan del Golfo and the ELN has displaced Indigenous families as far as Medellin, with reports of kidnappings and killings.

haiti|2026-11-06|cite soleil port au pri.text: 5–6 Nov — Cite Soleil, Port-au-Prince: Boston gang leader Mathias Saintil (Viv Ansanm) was killed in a security operation that a rights group says used explosive drones. PM Fils-Aime confirmed his death. The rights group reported five gang members killed and about 15 injured in that strike.

haiti|2026-11-05|port au prince|diplomat.text: 5 Nov — Port-au-Prince: The US Embassy in San Salvador formally protested what it called poor Salvadoran coordination, alleging Salvadoran gunfire struck the US Embassy compound in Haiti and nearly hit US personnel. El Salvador rejected the claim on 9 November.

haiti|2026-11-08|near port au prince|dro.actor: Haitian police drone task force / Salvadoran forces
haiti|2026-11-08|near port au prince|dro.text: 8 Nov — Near Port-au-Prince: An early-morning strike by the police drone task force, backed by contractors and Salvadoran helicopters, destroyed a house used by 400 Mawozo leader Wilson Joseph. He was not inside. Reports of up to 20 gunmen killed are unconfirmed, and rights groups and the UN have raised concerns about civilian harm.

haiti|ongoing|haiti|political.text: 8–10 Nov — Haiti: Wilson Joseph proposed 18 November as the start of negotiations. Rubio said El Salvador is operating separately from the international force, and the four Salvadoran technicians kidnapped on 18 October remain missing.

cuba|2026-11-07|el cobre santiago de cub.text: 7 Nov — Guamuta/El Cobre, Santiago de Cuba: Special forces and State Security raided the home of Yoel Alejandro Perez Serrano, who runs a free-meals project for more than 400 people, and detained him. Dozens of residents, including mothers with small children, marched through El Cobre demanding his release. His wife and some protesters were reportedly detained.

cuba|2026-11-08|el cobre|political.text: 8–9 Nov — El Cobre: Food trucks appeared in El Cobre and Guamuta the day after the protest. As of 9 November, Perez Serrano had not been released and authorities had not disclosed where he is held or any charges.

cuba|2026-11-04|nationwide|humanitarian.text: 4 Nov — Nationwide: The Electric Union forecast 960 MW available against peak demand of 2,850 MW, a generation deficit of about 1,890 MW with seven thermal units out of service.

ecuador|2026-11-08|manabi|armed-attack.text: 7–8 Nov — Manabi: Primicias reported 19 killings in three days across Montecristi, Manta, Bolivar, Portoviejo, Sucre, El Carmen, Pedernales and Jipijapa, including three people shot dead in Calceta on 7 November and two men killed in a house in Montecristi on 8 November. Manabi has recorded 1,018 violent deaths in 2026.

ecuador|2026-11-08|calceta manabi|armed-.text: 8 Nov — Calceta, Manabi: Local news-page journalist Tomas Beltran was shot dead outside his home. He had reported death threats and was in the prosecutor's witness-protection system; the Inter American Press Association condemned the killing.

ecuador|2026-11-09|guayaquil|armed-attac.text: 9 Nov — Guayaquil (via a la Costa km 22): Gunmen attacked a pickup truck at the entrance to a residential development, killing two women.

ecuador|2026-11-10|guayas manabi los rio.place: Guayas, Manabi, Los Rios, El Oro, Esmeraldas
ecuador|2026-11-10|guayas manabi los rio.text: 8–10 Nov — Guayas, Manabi, Los Rios, El Oro, Esmeraldas: The Interior Ministry reported 2,292 people captured in the curfew's first week, with 204 firearms and 612 kg of drugs seized. The fourth curfew of 2026 ended at 05:00 on 10 November, ahead of the 29 November local elections.

peru|ongoing|lima callao|armed-attack.text: Week to 7 Nov — Lima/Callao: America TV counted six extortion attacks on public transport and three deaths in a week, in districts including San Juan de Lurigancho, Callao, Villa El Salvador, Surquillo, Carabayllo and Chorrillos, including bus driver Josue Perdomo Estrada, shot six times in Chorrillos. The Public Ministry recorded 169 extortion attacks on transport companies (95 dead) between January and October 2026.

peru|2026-11-10|lima|unrest.text: 10 Nov — Lima: More than 50 public transport companies suspended service for a march from Plaza de Acho to Congress against extortion and driver killings, threatening a strike if the government does not act. Heavy-cargo hauliers separately announced a 72-hour national strike for 16–18 November over diesel prices.

peru|2026-11-11|lima callao|other.text: 11 Nov — Lima/Callao: Pope Leo XIV's visit began under a security plan of more than 37,000 police nationwide (22,464 in Lima and Callao) and drone-flight restrictions in six cities through 16 November.

bolivia|2026-11-06|patacamaya|military-a.text: 6–7 Nov — Patacamaya/La Paz: Police deployed 450 officers to control Patacamaya and eight entry points to La Paz ahead of the Morales-aligned march called for 6 November. Police reported no irregularities and normal traffic, and no blockades or clashes were reported.

bolivia|2026-11-11|la paz|political.text: 11 Nov — La Paz: Government Minister Marco Antonio Oviedo called Evo Morales 'the chief of a cartel' trafficking drugs from the Chapare (Tropico de Cochabamba). He said police detected more than 8 million bolivianos moving from the Tropico to finance the May–June blockades, which left 16 dead.

bolivia|2026-11-12|la paz|political.text: 12 Nov — La Paz: Defence Minister Ernesto Justiniano said the armed forces are being prepared to confront 'narcoterrorism' in support of, not in place of, the police, citing lessons from the 53-day crisis.

dominican republic|2026-11-10|santo domi.text: 10 Nov — Santo Domingo: President Abinader confirmed that the Dominican Republic provides logistics and intelligence to Salvadoran forces fighting gangs in Haiti and urged better coordination between them and the GSF. He said the southern border has been reinforced and gang activity remains concentrated in and around Port-au-Prince.

dominican republic|2026-11-04|dajabon el.text: 4 Nov — Dajabon, Elias Pina, Jimani, Pedernales: The Defence Minister toured four crossings and called the border 'totally calm'. About 11,000 troops are deployed along the frontier, and the government says it could close the border if needed.

jamaica|2026-11-08|st elizabeth|armed-at.text: 8 Nov — St Elizabeth (Monymusk and Williamsfield areas): In predawn operations, security forces fatally shot two murder suspects, Dadrian White and Oshane Wright, in two separate 'alleged confrontations' about 45 minutes apart. Police say two firearms were recovered.

jamaica|2026-11-04|st elizabeth|armed-at.text: 4 Nov — St Elizabeth: A man was fatally shot by a licensed firearm holder at a bar.

jamaica|2026-11-03|manchester|armed-atta.text: 3 Nov — Manchester: Police said a man killed in a firefight with officers was on his way to carry out a contract killing, the third police killing in Manchester and St Catherine in about a week.

gaza|2026-11-12|khan younis nasser hospi.text: 12 Nov — Khan Younis (Nasser Hospital): An Israeli air strike on the hospital killed six people, including a surgeon and a 13-year-old boy, according to the Health Ministry; the IDF said it targeted the Hamas Khan Younis brigade commander. Israeli fire killed 11 people across Gaza that day.

gaza|2026-11-14|al mawasi khan younis|ai.text: 14 Nov — al-Mawasi (Khan Younis): An Israeli air strike killed Samir Abu Younis, commander of Hamas's Rafah Brigade, as confirmed by the IDF, Shin Bet and Hamas; others were wounded.

gaza|2026-11-17|gaza strip|armed-attack.text: 17 Nov — Gaza Strip: Israeli fire killed six Palestinians, including a six-year-old boy, according to the civil defence agency and hospitals cited by AFP.

gaza|2026-11-18|central gaza salah al di.place: Central Gaza (Salah al-Din Street, east of Nuseirat / north of Bureij)
gaza|2026-11-18|central gaza salah al di.text: 18 Nov — Central Gaza (Salah al-Din Street, east of Nuseirat / north of Bureij): Israel launched its first publicly announced ground operation since the October 2025 ceasefire, west of the Yellow Line, citing Hamas violations. Attacks in al-Mughraqa, Deir el-Balah, Nuseirat and Gaza City killed at least four people, and the Health Ministry's post-ceasefire toll reached 1,658.

lebanon|2026-11-15|southern lebanon|mili.text: 15 Nov — Southern Lebanon: The IDF said it demolished a Hezbollah tunnel in the south.

lebanon|2026-11-16|janta bekaa syria leb.text: 16 Nov — Janta (Bekaa, Syria–Lebanon border): The Israeli military said it struck overnight a weapons shipment moving from Syria to Hezbollah; no casualty figures were reported.

lebanon|2026-11-18|qantara marjayoun dis.text: 18 Nov — Qantara (Marjayoun district): An Israeli air strike hit the town, according to Al Jazeera; no casualties were reported. The same day, Defence Minister Katz said Israel will keep occupying parts of Lebanon until armed groups are dismantled.

lebanon|2026-11-18|washington|political.text: 18 Nov — Washington: The US Treasury sanctioned Hezbollah-linked targets, including a charity and a gold and cash smuggling network.

iran|2026-11-13|bahrain|drone-strike.text: 13–17 Nov — Bahrain: Iran attacked US facilities in Bahrain three times in five days, citing US drone surveillance and an attack on Iranian communications towers. The IRGC said it fired six drones at a US radar at the Riffa helicopter base on 15 Nov and targeted a US radar at Isa Air Base on 17 Nov; US officials said all attacks were intercepted, and CENTCOM said no US personnel were injured.

iran|2026-11-17|qeshm island|airstrike.text: 17 Nov — Qeshm Island: A US fighter jet struck an IRGC missile launch site in what US officials called self-defence in response to the Bahrain radar attack; an Iranian regional official said there was no serious damage.

iran|2026-11-15|strait of hormuz|maritim.text: 15–18 Nov — Strait of Hormuz: UKMTO reported near-daily tanker attacks. A tanker was hit approaching the strait on 15 Nov and another was hit in the engine room on 16 Nov. An ADNOC vessel was struck on 17 Nov (one crew member missing, 11 injured), and a tanker was hit north of Khasab on 18 Nov (crew safe). The IRGC claimed several tankers hit mines and that a VLCC sank (unverified).

iran|2026-11-18|ali al salem air base ku.text: 18 Nov — Ali Al Salem Air Base (Kuwait): Iran's army said its drones hit US Patriot systems and drone and missile launch platforms; Kuwait said its air defences intercepted the drones, and its Foreign Ministry condemned a 'dangerous escalation'. It was the first attack on Kuwait in more than two months.

yemen|2026-11-15|dhubab bab al mandeb ta.text: 15 Nov — Dhubab / Bab al-Mandeb (Taiz governorate): Government-aligned forces, including the Southern Armed Forces, withdrew from Dhubab airport and the surrounding area to reinforce Aden, leaving the Houthis in control of the strait's Yemeni coast. Reports put Houthi forces at Tor al-Baha, about 60–80 km from Aden.

yemen|2026-11-17|sanaa amran saada hodei.text: 17 Nov — Sanaa / Amran / Saada / Hodeidah: The Saudi-led coalition said it struck 60 military targets, including missile tunnels and drone workshops. Houthi health officials said at least 17 people were killed, including 15 in a strike on a sponge factory in Hodeidah and two in Kitaf (Saada).

yemen|2026-11-17|marib|shelling.text: 17 Nov (reported) — Marib: Houthi shelling of a displaced persons camp reportedly killed two children and injured 15; government forces said they carried out four air strikes on Houthi positions and missile launchers in Marib.

yemen|2026-11-15|taiz lahj marib al jawf.text: 15 Nov — Taiz / Lahj / Marib / al-Jawf: Government spokesman al-Nuzaili claimed 321 Houthi leaders were killed or wounded in 723 targeted operations under 'Operation Dawn of Yemen' (unverified); the Houthis fired missiles and drones toward Riyadh, the Eastern Province and Mecca under a 'siege for siege' principle.

israel|2026-11-17|al duyuk al tahta near.text: 17 Nov — al-Duyuk al-Tahta (near Jericho, West Bank): Settlers shot dead a 72-year-old Palestinian woman in front of her home near a newly established outpost; Wafa reported 10 others wounded. The IDF said there were Israeli and Palestinian casualties.

israel|2026-11-14|sa ir west bank|unrest.text: 14 Nov — Sa'ir (south of Hebron, West Bank): Dozens of masked settlers attacked Palestinians harvesting olives, injuring at least five according to WAFA; the IDF condemned the attackers.

israel|2026-11-15|tel aviv herzliya|poli.text: 15 Nov — Tel Aviv / Herzliya: Yashar and Likud teams opened unity-government talks under Eisenkot's mandate (deadline 6 December); a Haaretz photojournalist said he was beaten by right-wing activists at a protest outside Eisenkot's home.

israel|2026-11-18|tel aviv|military-acti.text: 18 Nov — Tel Aviv: CENTCOM commander Adm. Brad Cooper met IDF Chief of Staff Zamir and Mossad Director Gofman, amid reported US–Israeli debate on whether to restart larger military action against Iran.

iraq|2026-11-17|sulaymaniyah|drone-strik.text: 17 Nov — Sulaymaniyah: Two explosives-laden drones attacked bases of Iranian Kurdish opposition groups, according to Reuters; no casualties were reported. Iran has repeatedly struck such bases.

iraq|2026-11-16|jurf al sakhar babil pro.text: 16–17 Nov — Jurf al-Sakhar (Babil province): PM Ali al-Zaidi said security forces would enter the Kataib Hezbollah stronghold over an alleged oil-smuggling network. Kataib Hezbollah vowed to fight if they do, and al-Zaidi dismissed nine Babil security and administrative officials, including the police chief.

iraq|2026-11-16|baghdad|diplomatic.text: 16 Nov — Baghdad: IRGC Quds Force commander Esmail Qaani reportedly arrived to mediate between Kataib Hezbollah and the government.

iraq|2026-11-17|kirkuk ceyhan pipeline|o.text: 17 Nov — Kirkuk–Ceyhan pipeline: Iraq resumed oil exports to Turkey at an initial 120,000 barrels per day after the line had been largely idle since 2023.

saudi arabia|2026-11-15|riyadh eastern p.text: 15 Nov — Riyadh / Eastern Province: Air defences intercepted two Houthi ballistic missiles aimed at the capital, and the coalition reported three drones downed over the Eastern Province.

saudi arabia|2026-11-18|riyadh|missile-s.text: 18 Nov — Riyadh: Air defences intercepted two Houthi cruise missiles fired toward Riyadh, and alerts sounded in three other Saudi cities. The Houthis claimed hits on King Khalid International Airport and a financial centre, and the coalition said it destroyed a Houthi launch platform.

saudi arabia|2026-11-19|riyadh|missile-s.text: 19 Nov — Riyadh: A Houthi missile was intercepted over the capital at about 04:45 after a civil defence alert; coalition spokesman al-Maliki said debris fell and material damage was being assessed.

saudi arabia|2026-11-11|saudi arabia|mil.text: 11 Nov — Saudi Arabia: Egypt's Foreign Minister said Egyptian forces had been in the kingdom for months helping defend 'sensitive' sites; Egypt confirmed troops, armour, anti-aircraft batteries and surface-to-surface missiles. Reuters reported on 18 Nov that Riyadh is preparing for the Yemen war to last into 2027.

syria|2026-11-14|jaramana damascus count.text: 14 Nov — Jaramana (Damascus countryside): An explosive device planted in a car detonated near a battery factory, killing a man and his young daughter and seriously injuring his wife, according to SANA. It was the second deadly bombing in Jaramana in just over three months, and no one claimed it.

syria|2026-11-15|jabata al khashab qunei.text: 15 Nov — Jabata al-Khashab (Quneitra): Israeli forces raided homes and shops and detained two people, according to SANA.

syria|2026-11-18|al samdaniya al sharqiy.text: 18 Nov — al-Samdaniya al-Sharqiya (Quneitra): Israeli forces entered the village with three military vehicles under reconnaissance aircraft, according to state media; on 17 Nov Damascus demanded international action to halt incursions in Quneitra and Daraa.

syria|2026-11-11|quneitra countryside|mi.text: 11 Nov — Quneitra countryside: Israeli forces expelled olive harvesters from farmland and set agricultural land on fire, according to Syrian media; SOHR counted 35 Israeli incursions and movements in the south between 1 and 7 Nov.

egypt|2026-11-09|cairo|military-activity.text: 9–11 Nov — Cairo: Foreign Minister Abdelatty confirmed that Egyptian forces had deployed to Saudi Arabia months before parliamentary approval and are being reinforced to help defend 'sensitive' sites; Egypt confirmed troops, armour, anti-aircraft batteries and surface-to-surface missiles. Middle East Eye, citing military sources, reported a Rafale squadron and warships moved toward Bab el-Mandeb (unconfirmed).

egypt|2026-11-16|tripoli libya|diplomati.text: 16 Nov — Tripoli (Libya): PM Dbeibah met Egypt's intelligence chief to discuss security cooperation, according to LANA.

jordan|2026-11-15|amman state security c.text: 15 Nov — Amman (State Security Court): The court sentenced three men to death by hanging for the 23 Oct Karak church attack (nine killed), convicting them on nine counts of premeditated murder for terrorist purposes.

jordan|2026-11-11|amman|political.text: 11 Nov — Amman: Prosecutors charged the ex-convict suspect in the 5 Nov killing of police Corporal Jawad al-Salaytah under the 2006 Anti-Terrorism Law and referred him to the State Security Court; the two attacks have renewed debate on counter-terrorism legislation and on releasing terrorism convicts.

libya|2026-11-14|tripoli eastern libya|d.text: 14 Nov — Tripoli / eastern Libya: AFRICOM commander Gen. Dagvin Anderson met PM Dbeibah and Saddam Haftar separately to discuss military unification, border security, counter-terrorism and the Flintlock 2027 exercise; US adviser Boulos warned spoilers of the 4+4 unification framework of sanctions.

libya|2026-11-14|zintan|political.text: 14–16 Nov — Zintan: The House of Representatives accused the GNU of blocking its planned session in Zintan, and UNSMIL expressed regret that the session failed.

libya|2026-11-16|tripoli|diplomatic.text: 16 Nov — Tripoli: Dbeibah met Egypt's intelligence chief on security cooperation; no armed clashes were found in reporting for 12–19 Nov.

ukraine|2026-11-16|kyiv|missile-strike.text: 16–17 Nov — Kyiv: Russian ballistic missiles struck the Northern and Southern bridges over the Dnipro; Zelensky said four missiles targeted the Southern and three the Northern bridge. Both bridges were closed, two people were killed in Obolon and critical infrastructure was hit, causing water and heating disruption. In the same attack Zaporizhzhia's Preobrazhenskyi bridge was hit and two people were killed there with 31 injured, Smila was struck by eight ballistic missiles, and about 700,000 households lost power in Dnipropetrovsk Oblast (Kyiv Independent, Euromaidan Press).

ukraine|2026-11-18|odesa|missile-strike.text: 18 Nov — Odesa: Russian strikes hit the historic centre in three waves, killing four people, including in the UNESCO-protected zone. Reuters cited at least seven injured and Al Jazeera 13. Zelensky called the attack 'brutal and deliberate' and said follow-up strikes targeted first responders and police already at the scene.

ukraine|2026-11-14|kostiantynivka dobrop.text: 14 Nov — Kostiantynivka–Dobropillia axes (Donetsk Oblast): ISW assessed that recent Russian mechanised assaults and a high tempo of attacks show Moscow prioritising the southern flank of the 'Fortress Belt', and reported that the Kremlin is requesting a temporary local ceasefire in Kostiantynivka that would likely help Russian forces reinforce. Elsewhere, Russian forces advanced northeast of Lyman and east of Sloviansk, while Ukrainian forces advanced south of Novopavlivka.

ukraine|2026-11-12|dublin baldonnel|dipl.text: 12 Nov — Dublin (Baldonnel): Zelensky met US envoys Witkoff and Kushner hours after they had briefed Putin in Moscow. Kushner said Putin had agreed to European participation in the next round, and Zelensky called the prisoner exchange agreed in Abu Dhabi the largest of the war. On 17 November Zelensky said Ukraine would hand its exchange proposals to the US at a meeting with American and European partners in Berlin on 19 November.

russia|2026-11-16|kerch bridge crimea|mi.text: 16–17 Nov — Kerch Bridge (Crimea): A Ukrainian drone and missile strike sent the main road arch of the bridge into the Kerch Strait, leaving a gap in the roadway; Reuters verified the video. The parallel rail bridge stayed up and Russia's Transport Ministry said rail traffic resumed on one track. Al Jazeera reported two people killed. Zelensky called it an 'unprecedented' operation in seven stages over several weeks, and Russia's Investigative Committee opened a terrorism case.

russia|2026-11-16|moscow and 15 other re.text: 16 Nov — Moscow and 15 other regions: Russia's Defence Ministry claimed it downed 1,336 Ukrainian drones overnight across 16 regions, Crimea and the Azov and Black seas, the largest count of the war (unverified). Mayor Sobyanin said about 600 were aimed at Moscow. Local authorities reported one person killed by Ukrainian drones in Belgorod Oblast, and Ukraine's military said it hit an oil depot in Azov (Rostov Oblast).

russia|2026-11-17|krasnodar krai|drone-s.text: 17–18 Nov — Krasnodar Krai: Ukraine's General Staff said it struck storage tanks at the Ilsky refinery and a processing unit at the Afipsky refinery; Kyiv Post counts this as the eighth attack on Afipsky this year. Russian officials confirmed attacks on two industrial facilities without details, and authorities have urged oil companies to produce more lower-grade gasoline to avert shortages.

russia|2026-11-18|shenzhen china|diploma.text: 18–19 Nov — Shenzhen (China): Putin attended the APEC summit, where China confirmed the first Trump–Xi–Putin trilateral meeting. Kremlin aide Ushakov said Ukraine would likely be discussed, while a White House official said Trump would not raise it. No substantive outcome on Ukraine had been reported at the time of writing.

belarus|2026-11-16|belarus location unsp.text: 16 Nov — Belarus (location unspecified): Lukashenko ordered an unscheduled combat-readiness inspection of State Border Committee rapid-response units, per Security Council State Secretary Volfovich via Belta. It includes field exercises in which units march and repel simulated attacks by enemy sabotage and reconnaissance groups; the location and duration were not specified.

moldova|2026-11-17|chis ina u|military-a.text: 17 Nov — Chișinău: Several Russian drones violated Moldovan airspace, President Sandu said, one of them a Shahed/Geran-type drone over the capital that alarmed residents. The Defence Ministry recorded two violations, per Reuters. Airspace was closed from 16:27 local time for about half an hour, and police received reports of loud bangs in Chișinău and Florești. No casualties were reported.

moldova|2026-11-18|chis ina u|diplomatic.text: 18 Nov — Chișinău: The Foreign Ministry summoned Russian ambassador Oleg Ozerov to protest the airspace violations, which Foreign Minister Popșoi called a 'serious breach of our sovereignty'. Russia rejects Moldova's accusations and says no proof has been given that the drones were Russian.

georgia|2026-11-11|batumi|political.text: 11–17 Nov — Batumi: The Constitutional Court's hearings on Georgian Dream's petition to ban five opposition parties went through their question stage, which the court chairman said would run until 17 November. On 11 November Chairman Nadaraia removed Coalition for Change leaders Nika Gvaramia and Maia Kopaleishvili from the courtroom. The court has rejected nearly all of some 14 opposition motions; no ruling had been issued, and the legal deadline is 24 June 2027.

georgia|2026-11-14|tbilisi|political.text: 14 Nov — Tbilisi: Tbilisi City Court sentenced security officers to five years each for abuse of authority with violence over the May 2024 beating of opposition politician Levan Khabeishvili, after a closed-door trial with undisclosed defendant names (SOVA). Khabeishvili's lawyer says the special-forces chief bears primary responsibility.

georgia|2026-11-15|tbilisi|unrest.text: 15–17 Nov — Tbilisi: Pro-European protests outside parliament reached their 720th consecutive day, with at least 200 people demanding an amnesty for protest prisoners and the repeal of repressive laws (Caucasian Knot). Organisers are preparing a mass rally for the 28 November anniversary.

armenia|2026-11-12|dublin|diplomatic.text: 12 Nov — Dublin: Pashinyan and Aliyev met on the sidelines of the 9th European Political Community summit and discussed transport links, trade, border delimitation and confidence-building on the basis of the August 2025 Washington Declaration.

armenia|2026-11-17|yerevan|political.text: 17–18 Nov — Yerevan: Speaker Rubinyan said Armenia rejects Baku's demand for a new constitution as a precondition and is 'ready to sign even today'. Pashinyan said guarantees exist for signing and ratification once a new constitution is adopted, and has said the treaty could be signed in 2027–2028.

armenia|2026-11-18|yerevan|political.text: 18 Nov — Yerevan: Strong Armenia faction leader Narek Karapetyan said the opposition would block the referendum if it saw division or a threat to sovereignty. A 13-force opposition bloc, including Strong Armenia, Kocharyan's Armenia Alliance, the ARF and the Republican Party, has formed to reject what it calls the 'Aliyev constitution'. On 11 November the Anti-Corruption Court let prosecutors pursue expanded charges against Narek Karapetyan.

azerbaijan|2026-11-12|dublin|diplomatic.text: 12 Nov — Dublin: Aliyev met Pashinyan at the European Political Community summit to discuss implementing the Washington Declaration (transport route, trade, delimitation); Baku maintains it will not sign the initialled treaty until Armenia changes its constitution.

azerbaijan|2026-11-16|goytepe border det.text: 16 Nov — Goytepe border detachment (Iranian border): Border guards intercepted a drug-carrying paratrike flying in from Iran and detained its Iranian pilot, per the State Border Service.

azerbaijan|2026-11-17|horadiz and lankar.text: 17 Nov — Horadiz and Lankaran (Iranian border): Border guards prevented an attempt to smuggle about 50 kg of narcotics and 3,000 psychotropic pills from Iran, per APA.

mali|2026-11-14|8 10 km north of abei ba.place: 8–10 km north of Abeïbara, Kidal region
mali|2026-11-14|8 10 km north of abei ba.text: 14 Nov — 8–10 km north of Abeïbara, Kidal region: The army general staff said FAMa, supported by partners, struck a regrouping point with fighters, vehicles and a fuel depot. Reconnaissance was continuing; no toll was given.

mali|2026-11-16|33 km south west of se v.place: 33 km south-west of Sévaré, Mopti region
mali|2026-11-16|33 km south west of se v.text: 16 Nov — 33 km south-west of Sévaré, Mopti region: The army said it struck a logistics gathering including motorcycles, as part of Operation Dougoukoloko. No toll was given.

mali|2026-11-09|mopti se gou kidal timbu.place: Mopti, Ségou, Kidal, Timbuktu and Kayes regions
mali|2026-11-09|mopti se gou kidal timbu.text: 9–16 Nov — Mopti, Ségou, Kidal, Timbuktu and Kayes regions: JNIM's media wing claimed nine attacks in Mali against the army, allied militias, Dozo hunters and Russian Africa Corps personnel. The claims carry no tolls and cannot be verified.

mali|2026-11-16|bamako|military-activity.text: c. 16 Nov — Bamako: A new escorted convoy of 840 fuel tankers reached the capital, bringing November deliveries to 1,505 tankers under FAMa escort, according to official figures relayed by regional media.

niger|2026-11-12|tillim near te ra tilla.text: 12 Nov — Tillim, near Téra, Tillabéri region: Unidentified gunmen ambushed residents travelling to Téra's weekly market, killing at least 37 civilians; one more died of wounds the next day, bringing the reported toll to 38. Some reports attribute the attack to IS Sahel; no group has been officially named.

niger|2026-11-16|near kobague torodi dep.text: 16–17 Nov — Near Kobagué, Torodi department, Tillabéri: The National Guard said it dismantled a logistics base of armed groups in a night operation and 'neutralised' two people.

burkina faso|2026-11-09|bam mouhoun se n.place: Bam, Mouhoun, Séno, Gourma, Oudalan, Sanmatenga and Yatenga provinces
burkina faso|2026-11-09|bam mouhoun se n.text: 9–16 Nov — Bam, Mouhoun, Séno, Gourma, Oudalan, Sanmatenga and Yatenga provinces: JNIM's media wing claimed 11 attacks on army and VDP positions, checkpoints and patrols, including ambushes and IEDs. The claims cannot be independently verified.

burkina faso|ongoing|yabousgou|armed-att.text: Mid-Nov (date not given) — Yabousgou: JNIM claimed it overran a military position, killing seven soldiers, destroying a vehicle and seizing weapons and motorcycles. This rests only on the group's claim.

burkina faso|2026-11-13|oudalan northern.text: 13 Nov — Oudalan/northern border: Al Jazeera reported escalating battles between JNIM and IS Sahel along the Mali border. IS Sahel claimed more than 400 JNIM fighters killed around Ganadaouri on 9 Oct; i-Sahel counted at least 120 bodies in published images but could not verify them.

sudan|2026-11-17|ghubeish west kordofan|.text: 17 Nov — Ghubeish, West Kordofan: A drone strike on the Musab Bin Omair school sheltering displaced families killed at least 16 civilians and injured about 10, according to the Kordofan Observatory, which attributed it to the army. The toll is preliminary.

sudan|2026-11-15|abu qalb abu zabad loca.place: Abu Qalb, Abu Zabad locality, West Kordofan
sudan|2026-11-15|abu qalb abu zabad loca.text: 15 Nov — Abu Qalb, Abu Zabad locality, West Kordofan: A drone strike on a football field killed at least 15 civilians, including four children, according to the Kordofan Human Rights Observatory, which attributed it to the army. The RSF-aligned Tasis alliance gave a toll of nine; Dabanga could not verify the figures.

sudan|2026-11-13|west kordofan|ground-cl.text: 13–16 Nov — West Kordofan: The army and the Joint Force entered Al-Khuwai (13 Nov), took Al-Morkib, Khamasat and Umm Oweisha about 60 km east of Al-Nahud (14 Nov), and announced the capture of Al-Sa'atat north-east of Abu Zabad (16 Nov). The RSF still holds Al-Nahud and most of the state.

sudan|2026-11-13|dandaro blue nile|drone.text: 13 Nov — Dandaro, Blue Nile: The army said its air defences shot down a long-range drone that had crossed from Ethiopia. On 16 Nov it announced major reinforcements to the Blue Nile front, and the Kurmuk governor raised the toll of the 10 Nov Bani Shako drone strike to 16.

chad|2026-11-17|miski tibesti|drone-stri.text: 17 Nov — Miski, Tibesti: The Miski Self-Defence Committee said a drone strike it attributed to the government killed at least one civilian. The government did not respond to AFP; Miski remains under the committee's control.

mauritania|2026-11-13|nouakchott mali bo.text: 13 Nov — Nouakchott/Mali border: An analysis by the Spanish Institute for Strategic Studies (IEEE) named Mauritania as the Maghreb country most directly exposed to the deterioration in Mali, citing the porous border, the terrorist threat and the hosting of about 290,000 Malian refugees in Hodh Chargui. It noted Mauritania has suffered no attack since 2011.

nigeria|2026-11-15|sabuwar kaura kaura n.place: Sabuwar Kaura, Kaura Namoda LGA, Zamfara
nigeria|2026-11-15|sabuwar kaura kaura n.text: 15 Nov — Sabuwar Kaura, Kaura Namoda LGA, Zamfara: About 30 bandits, allegedly loyal to Bello Wakkala, attacked a mosque, killing seven worshippers including an aide to Governor Dauda Lawal and abducting 15, according to Daily Trust. Police gave a lower toll of one dead and four abducted. A separate attack on a home in the town on 16 Nov killed a guard.

nigeria|2026-11-15|zwagal jipal district.place: Zwagal, Jipal district, Mangu LGA, Plateau
nigeria|2026-11-15|zwagal jipal district.text: 15 Nov — Zwagal, Jipal district, Mangu LGA, Plateau: Gunmen attacked the village at night; nine victims were buried in a mass grave, and two more men were killed in an ambush in Bokkos LGA, bringing the toll to at least 11 (The Sun). The village head said the attackers spoke Fulani.

nigeria|2026-11-12|kerenoa marte lga bor.text: 12 Nov — Kerenoa, Marte LGA, Borno: Air strikes on a suspected ISWAP hideout reportedly killed at least ten fighters, including attendees of a commanders' meeting, according to military-sourced reports. Not independently verified.

nigeria|2026-11-16|monguno and arinna so.place: Monguno and Arinna (South Lake Chad), Borno
nigeria|2026-11-16|monguno and arinna so.text: 16–17 Nov — Monguno and Arinna (South Lake Chad), Borno: Operation Hadin Kai said air strikes killed 21 ISWAP fighters, including named leaders, and injured ten. The claim is not independently verified.

north korea|2026-11-15|samjiyon ryanggan.text: 15–16 Nov — Samjiyon, Ryanggang: KCNA showed Kim Jong Un with his daughter Ju Ae touring the Samjiyon airport reconstruction, a tourist railway and a ski resort. He made no response to Trump's repeated public calls to meet him in China during the APEC summit (NBC, Euronews).

north korea|2026-11-18|kim jong suk nava.place: Kim Jong Suk Naval University, South Hamgyong
north korea|2026-11-18|kim jong suk nava.text: 18 Nov — Kim Jong Suk Naval University, South Hamgyong: During two days of field guidance in South Hamgyong, Kim criticised the naval activities of 'wicked enemies' and said the university's primary duty is to train professional naval commanders (KCNA via NK News).

north korea|2026-11-14|moscow|diplomatic.text: 14 Nov — Moscow: Senior party secretary Jo Yong Won arrived in Moscow for talks with Dmitry Medvedev, days before the Xi–Trump–Putin meeting in Shenzhen (state media via NK News).

north korea|ongoing|north korea|military.text: 12–19 Nov — North Korea: No missile launch was found for the period. The last confirmed launch remains the 4 November salvo from Sondok.

myanmar|2026-11-13|byar la idp camp ponn.place: Byar La IDP camp, Ponnagyun Township, Rakhine
myanmar|2026-11-13|byar la idp camp ponn.text: 13 Nov — Byar La IDP camp, Ponnagyun Township, Rakhine: Regime fighter jets bombed a displacement camp northeast of Sittwe without warning, killing 12 people, including a five-year-old, and injuring 18, according to witnesses and a rescue service (AFP). BNI gave an early toll of at least eight.

myanmar|2026-11-15|ye township mon state.text: 15–16 Nov — Ye Township, Mon State (NMSP area): Regime aircraft dropped two bombs on Kyae Daik village on 16 Nov, killing two civilians and injuring 14. Overnight bombing of Hlan Chaung Wa village, including from a Y-12 aircraft, killed one more and injured three (m.CDM).

myanmar|2026-11-13|myaing and mindon tow.text: 13–14 Nov — Myaing and Mindon townships, Magway: The Myaing PDF said two children were killed after two days of regime airstrikes and drone attacks. On 16 Nov a fighter-jet strike on two villages in Mindon Township killed one civilian (m.CDM).

myanmar|2026-11-13|rakhine|ground-clash.text: 13–14 Nov — Rakhine: On the third anniversary of renewed fighting, the Arakan Army vowed to capture the three remaining regime-held townships, Sittwe, Kyaukphyu and Manaung (Mizzima). A resistance digest reported that the regime destroyed four bridges leading to besieged Kyaukphyu on 14 Nov. This is unverified.

pakistan|2026-11-12|kanak area mastung b.text: 12 Nov — Kanak area, Mastung, Balochistan: A vehicle-borne suicide attack struck an FC post. Police said forces repelled it and killed three attackers. The blast killed two civilians, injured three FC personnel and damaged homes and a mosque. The BLA's Majeed Brigade claimed it and says 18 personnel died, which is unverified.

pakistan|2026-11-13|balochistan and nort.text: 13–14 Nov — Balochistan and North Waziristan: ISPR said an armed-quadcopter attack on army patrol vehicles in Balochistan killed Maj. Omer Minhas Nasir and Havildar Muhammad Adnan Khan, and the BLA claimed a drone strike near Mastung. Two more soldiers died in North Waziristan operations that ISPR says killed 16 militants, while eight more militants were killed near Kolpur.

pakistan|2026-11-13|bannu khyber pakhtun.text: 13–18 Nov — Bannu, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa: Police said they foiled an attack on the Kingar Pul checkpoint, killing four militants they described as 'Fitna al-Khawarij' (TTP). On 18 Nov security forces killed four more in an operation in the Gidar Camp area.

pakistan|2026-11-13|kp and balochistan|m.text: 13 Nov — KP and Balochistan: The military said 74 militants had been killed in raids along the Afghan border since 3 Nov. Border clashes with the Afghan Taliban continue without a ceasefire.

india|2026-11-13|new heaven imphal ukhru.place: New Heaven, Imphal–Ukhrul road (NH-202), Ukhrul district, Manipur
india|2026-11-13|new heaven imphal ukhru.text: 13 Nov — New Heaven, Imphal–Ukhrul road (NH-202), Ukhrul district, Manipur: Suspected militants fired on two vehicles, killing four Naga civilians: a mother and son and two siblings. Police suspect Kuki militants, and a Kuki body in Ukhrul denied involvement. It was the fourth ambush on the Litan–New Heaven stretch.

india|ongoing|manipur|unrest.text: Mid-Nov — Manipur: The Ukhrul killings triggered a statewide shutdown and confrontations between protesters and security forces. Tangkhul civil-society groups gave the state and central governments a three-day ultimatum to flush out Kuki armed groups from Naga areas, and security forces began search and cordon operations.

india|2026-11-16|laroo kulgam jammu and.text: 16 Nov — Laroo, Kulgam, Jammu and Kashmir: An encounter killed LeT associate Umar Nisar Dar after LeT commander Mohammad Lateef Bhat escaped the cordon. Reports differ on whether one or two militants died.

india|2026-11-18|zangalpora devsar kulga.place: Zangalpora, Devsar, Kulgam, Jammu and Kashmir
india|2026-11-18|zangalpora devsar kulga.text: 18 Nov — Zangalpora, Devsar, Kulgam, Jammu and Kashmir: Security forces killed LeT commander Mohammad Lateef Bhat, whom agencies described as the last known active local militant in Kashmir, days after the 11 Nov attack on a CRPF patrol.

china|2026-11-18|shenzhen|diplomatic.text: 18–19 Nov — Shenzhen: China hosted the APEC leaders' meeting. Trump arrived on 18 Nov and began talks with Xi on 19 Nov ahead of the first Xi–Trump–Putin trilateral meeting, which was expected to cover Iran, Ukraine and nuclear proliferation. Readouts were not yet available.

china|2026-11-18|beijing|political.text: 18 Nov — Beijing: The Taiwan Affairs Office said Taiwan is 'a purely internal' matter, a day before the trilateral, without saying whether it would be discussed. Trump said in Manila that Xi would raise it.

china|2026-11-09|around taiwan|military-.text: 9–15 Nov — Around Taiwan: PLA air activity fell to 60 sorties (37 entering the ADIZ), down about 46% from the previous week's 111, with a 'joint combat readiness patrol' on 12 Nov (Taiwan Security Monitor), as the early-November 100-plus-ship surge wound down.

china|2026-11-13|beijing|diplomatic.text: 13 Nov — Beijing: Foreign Minister Wang Yi met South Korea's Cho Hyun. Seoul says China agreed to work toward bringing North Korea back to talks (Korea JoongAng Daily).

taiwan|2026-11-09|around taiwan|military.text: 9–15 Nov — Around Taiwan: The MND recorded 60 PLA aircraft sorties (37 entering the ADIZ), down from 111 the week before, with median-line crossings on 10, 12, 13 and 15 Nov and 'joint air-sea training' (a joint combat readiness patrol) on 12 Nov (Taiwan Security Monitor).

taiwan|2026-11-12|around taiwan|military.text: 12–14 Nov — Around Taiwan: The MND tracked seven PLA aircraft, seven warships and two official ships in the 24 hours to 12 Nov, and 10 aircraft, eight warships and three official ships to 14 Nov, when four fighters crossed the median line. One count gave 184 aircraft and 141 naval vessel detections for the month to 14 Nov (Taiwan News).

taiwan|2026-11-18|beijing shenzhen|polit.text: 18 Nov — Beijing / Shenzhen: Ahead of the Xi–Trump–Putin meeting, China's Taiwan Affairs Office called Taiwan 'a purely internal' matter. Trump said in Manila that he would not have to raise Taiwan because Xi would.

philippines|2026-11-18|manila|diplomatic.text: 18 Nov — Manila: Trump met Marcos at Malacañang before flying to Shenzhen. He said the South China Sea confrontations with China 'will be taken care of' and that the US was expanding defence cooperation, but announced no new treaty commitment (DPA). A trade deal was announced without disclosed terms.

philippines|2026-11-15|philippines|diplo.text: 15–17 Nov — Philippines: The 49th ASEAN Summit hosted by Manila ended without concluding the South China Sea Code of Conduct, missing the 2026 deadline. Manila says 80% of the text is agreed, and talks pass to Singapore's chairmanship (CNBC, Asia Times).

philippines|2026-11-16|central mindanao.place: Central Mindanao (Maguindanao del Norte, Maguindanao del Sur, Cotabato)
philippines|2026-11-16|central mindanao.text: 16 Nov — Central Mindanao (Maguindanao del Norte, Maguindanao del Sur, Cotabato): Four separate ambushes by unidentified gunmen killed three people, including retired soldier Danny Lakim in Datu Odin Sinsuat, and wounded four, among them Barangay Tumbras captain Fatima Mokamad (Philstar).

philippines|2026-11-19|west philippine s.text: 19 Nov — West Philippine Sea: PCG spokesman Jay Tarriela said the situation was generally calm despite the continued presence of CCG, maritime militia and other Chinese vessels in the EEZ, with no significant harassment of Filipino vessels recently (Daily Tribune).

south korea|2026-11-13|beijing|diplomati.text: 13 Nov — Beijing: Foreign Minister Cho Hyun asked Wang Yi to help bring Pyongyang back to the table, and Seoul says China agreed. Seoul also warned Washington and Beijing that a US–China–Russia meeting 'must not become a second Yalta' that recognises North Korea as a nuclear state (Korea JoongAng Daily).

south korea|2026-11-18|shenzhen|diplomat.text: 18–19 Nov — Shenzhen: President Lee attended APEC, where a summit with Xi was scheduled. NK News reported that Xi backed Seoul's push for US–North Korea dialogue during the meeting, while the presidential office said the future of US–North Korea dialogue remained 'unknown territory'.

vietnam|2026-11-18|shenzhen|diplomatic.text: 18–19 Nov — Shenzhen: General Secretary and State President To Lam met Xi Jinping on the sidelines of APEC, and the two sides exchanged views on maritime issues while Code of Conduct talks remain unresolved (Asia Times).

vietnam|2026-11-15|asean summit philippi.text: 15–17 Nov — ASEAN Summit, Philippines: The summit ended without concluding the South China Sea Code of Conduct, missing the 2026 deadline. Vietnam, a claimant state, faces continued Chinese construction in the Paracels and its own Spratly fortification drive, which Bloomberg links to a growing risk of a clash. No Vietnam–China maritime incident was found for 12–19 Nov.

japan|2026-11-11|yonaguni taiwan gap|mil.text: 11–12 Nov — Yonaguni–Taiwan gap: According to Japan's Joint Staff, a Chinese Y-9 electronic-intelligence aircraft and a suspected Chinese UAV flew from the East China Sea between Yonaguni and Taiwan into the Philippine Sea, prompting ASDF scrambles (Zona Militar, Seoul Economic Daily).

japan|2026-11-09|senkaku islands|maritim.text: 9 Nov (latest found) — Senkaku Islands: The 9 Nov entry of four CCG ships into territorial waters off Kuba Island remains the most recent one found. Defense News (16 Nov) describes Chinese naval and coast-guard presence near Japan as 'normalised' since the 2025 diplomatic crisis, with Senkaku deployments at 'very high levels'.

indonesia|2026-11-13|dekai yahukimo high.text: 13 Nov — Dekai, Yahukimo, Highland Papua: A wood cutter was allegedly killed in an attack that police attribute to a TPNPB-OPM ('KKB') group. Damai Cartenz personnel said they came under fire on the way to the scene, and police are pursuing suspects (Kompas, Tribunnews).

indonesia|2026-11-14|oksibil pegunungan.text: 14 Nov — Oksibil, Pegunungan Bintang: The Damai Cartenz task force ran patrols on suspected armed-group crossing routes after the latest Yahukimo incidents.

thailand|2026-11-10|yala songkhla and sa.text: 10–11 Nov — Yala, Songkhla and Satun: In coordinated insurgent attacks on 13 sites, about 20 armed, masked men tied up five guards and bombed and burned the Yala subdistrict administrative organisation office and official vehicles in Mueang Yala. Other strikes hit five Yala districts, utility poles in Sadao and Chana (Songkhla) and a checkpoint in Thung Wa (Satun), where three students in a van were slightly hurt. ISOC Region 4 condemned the attacks (Thai PBS World).

bangladesh|2026-11-17|faridpur and gopal.text: 17 Nov — Faridpur and Gopalganj: A BNP activist was killed during a protest near Hasina's home district of Gopalganj (Reuters, police). Other reports name a BNP leader killed in Faridpur amid BNP–Awami League clashes, and a BNP lawmaker's house and BNP supporters' shops in Gopalganj were set on fire. The same night a crude bomb exploded outside Cultural Affairs Minister Nitai Roy Chowdhury's residence in Dhaka.

bangladesh|2026-11-18|pirojpur and tungi.text: 18 Nov — Pirojpur and Tungipara (Gopalganj): Arsonists set two buses on fire in Pirojpur, burning a bus company helper to death. A mob torched a police station and police vehicles in Tungipara, Hasina's hometown, after clashes with Awami League activists (Reuters).

bangladesh|2026-11-18|narail|armed-attac.text: 18–19 Nov — Narail: Two local BNP leaders were killed when Awami League activists attacked a BNP march (PTI via ThePrint).

bangladesh|2026-11-19|dhaka and chattogr.text: 19 Nov — Dhaka and Chattogram: The banned Awami League's nationwide 'lockdown', on the anniversary of Hasina's death sentence, opened with pre-dawn crude-bomb blasts in Dhaka. Arsonists set Muhammad Yunus's ancestral home in Panchlaish, Chattogram, on fire, and at least 37 Grameen Bank branches and offices have been targeted since 10 Nov. Police arrested 565 people in Dhaka in 24 hours, and BGB troops were deployed in sensitive districts.

sri lanka|2026-11-08|trincomalee|other.text: 8 Nov (report) — Trincomalee: Police said three suspects, including the alleged gunman, a legally discharged former army soldier arrested in Dikwella on 6 Nov, were in custody (Newswire, Ada Derana).

venezuela|2026-11-12|apure state|militar.text: 12 Nov — Apure state: The FANB strategic command (CEOFANB) announced a military deployment, reported as 'Operation Sovereignty and Peace', in three Apure municipalities to dismantle irregular-group logistics camps and clandestine airstrips. It follows the ELN Eastern War Front's 5 November confirmation that it holds a Colombian army second lieutenant seized in Arauca; official statements do not name the ELN.

venezuela|2026-11-13|caracas|political.text: 13 Nov — Caracas: The Rodriguez government and the opposition delegation of the 2015 National Assembly opened a fourth round of talks at the Gran Melia hotel, behind closed doors and with US backing. The agenda covers renewal of the Supreme Court, restructuring of the CNE and the law used to disqualify Maria Corina Machado, who is not taking part.

venezuela|2026-11-14|caracas|political.text: 14 Nov — Caracas: The government's Programme for Peace and Democratic Coexistence confirmed the release under precautionary measures of Italian-Venezuelan political prisoner Daniel Echenagucia, who then left the country. Foro Penal's latest count (to 9 November) is 321 political prisoners: 171 awaiting judgment and 150 convicted.

colombia|2026-11-12|tibu norte de santan.text: 12 Nov — Tibu, Norte de Santander (vereda Barco La Silla): Explosives dropped from drones killed four soldiers of Land Operations Battalion No. 10 and wounded two to five more. Military sources point to the ELN, though other armed groups operate in the area. President De la Espriella vowed 'they will pay' and ordered a full Public Force deployment.

colombia|2026-11-10|taraza antioquia|air.text: 10 Nov (disclosed by 15 Nov) — Taraza, Antioquia: The bombing announced on 10 November was 'Operation Nehemias' against the Clan del Golfo. The Defence Ministry reported 10 dead, while La FM reported eight members of the Manuel Alexander Ariza Gutierrez substructure killed. El Tiempo counts nine government bombings in its first 100 days, after the military acknowledged an unreported October strike in Cumaribo, Vichada.

colombia|2026-11-16|sardinata norte de s.text: 16 Nov — Sardinata, Norte de Santander (San Martin de Loba): Drones dropped explosives on several points of the village, reportedly including health and education facilities, and residents fled. The ELN's Northeastern War Front blamed FARC dissident Front 33. No casualties had been reported by 18 November.

colombia|2026-11-16|national|political.text: 16 Nov — National: The government outlined a counter-drone emergency plan covering 16 of 32 departments. The FIP has recorded 318 explosive-drone attacks between January and 1 October 2026, about 72% attributed to EMC dissidents and 23% to the ELN.

haiti|2026-11-18|canaan north of port au.text: 18 Nov — Canaan, north of Port-au-Prince: President Bukele said Salvadoran troops demolished the mansion of Taliban gang leader Jeff Larose ('Jeff Canaan'), releasing video of helicopters firing on it. It is unclear whether Larose was inside or killed. The UN-backed Gang Suppression Force said it was not involved, and Haitian police participation is unclear.

haiti|2026-11-17|port au prince|politica.text: 17 Nov — Port-au-Prince and other towns: Thousands of Haitians marched in support of Bukele and the Salvadoran troops. Haiti's justice minister said there is 'no date' for the Salvadoran forces to leave, as they are needed to back the police until elections next year.

haiti|2026-11-17|port au prince area|hum.text: 17 Nov — Port-au-Prince area: Reuters, citing the UN, reported that some 7,000 people have fled their homes around the area where the four Salvadoran soldiers went missing on 18 October; they remain unaccounted for. A separate report warned that more than 250,000 Haitian children are at risk of acute malnutrition as violence blocks aid.

haiti|ongoing|haiti|armed-attack.text: To 11 Nov — Haiti: ACLED counts more than 100 people killed during El Salvador's intervention, at least 26 of them civilians. Al Jazeera and AP put the toll of the 8 November strike on 400 Mawozo leader Wilson Joseph's compound at about 20. Joseph, who survived, had asked the UN for talks, but the government insists any dialogue follow its own roadmap.

cuba|2026-11-13|calabazar havana|unrest.text: 13 Nov — Calabazar and Las Canas, Boyeros (Havana): Dozens of residents, many of them young, blocked a bridge, set fire to rubbish and tyres, banged pots and chanted 'We want light!' after days with only one or two hours of electricity and water shortages. Police and officers put out the fire, power was restored shortly afterwards, and no arrests were reported (14ymedio).

cuba|2026-11-15|nationwide|humanitarian.text: 15 Nov — Nationwide: The Electric Union forecast availability of 970 MW against peak demand of 2,800 MW, a deficit of about 1,830 MW. The actual peak shortfall reached 1,878 MW on 14 November and 1,735 MW on 17 November.

cuba|2026-11-18|matanzas|political.text: 18 Nov — Matanzas: Historian Alina Barbara Lopez was detained outside the Provincial Court before a peaceful protest demanding a date for her long-suspended trial. The Cuban Observatory for Freedom of Expression says she has been detained several times this year when attempting her monthly protests.

cuba|2026-11-17|havana|political.text: 17 Nov — Havana: Ladies in White leader Berta Soler was questioned over a 7 November protest about water shortages in Lawton and warned that blocking a public road to protest is a crime. Food-aid organiser Yoel Perez Serrano, detained on 7 November in El Cobre, has not been reported released.

ecuador|2026-11-11|guayas manabi el oro.place: Guayas, Manabi, El Oro, Los Rios, Esmeraldas, Pichincha, Santa Elena, Santo Domingo
ecuador|2026-11-11|guayas manabi el oro.text: 11 Nov — Guayas, Manabi, El Oro, Los Rios, Esmeraldas, Pichincha, Santa Elena, Santo Domingo: President Noboa signed Executive Decree 532, renewing the state of exception for 'grave internal commotion' for 30 days (to about 13 December), without a curfew. The decree cited 322 intentional homicides in these provinces between 14 October and 1 November, 144 of them in Guayas, and the 29 November local elections.

ecuador|2026-11-15|machala el oro|armed-.text: 15 Nov — Machala, El Oro: A gunman on a motorcycle opened fire on a group of friends in the 24 de Septiembre neighbourhood, killing five people and wounding four.

ecuador|2026-11-15|playas guayas|armed-a.text: 15 Nov — Playas (General Villamil), Guayas: Gunmen attacked a birthday party at a nightclub, killing three people, including an active-duty police sergeant, and wounding six.

ecuador|2026-11-15|manabi guayas el oro.place: Manabi, Guayas, El Oro, Santa Elena
ecuador|2026-11-15|manabi guayas el oro.text: 15–17 Nov — Manabi, Guayas, El Oro, Santa Elena: La Republica counted at least 27 violent deaths in three days, including six killings in under 12 hours in the Manta–Montecristi area on 15 November and three more in Guayaquil the same afternoon. Police report 7,026 violent deaths nationally from 1 January to 9 November, 11.5% fewer than in 2025.

peru|2026-11-17|jicamarca san juan de lu.text: 17 Nov — Jicamarca, San Juan de Lurigancho (Lima): Gunmen posing as passengers shot dead Los Mandarinos bus driver Jose Miranda more than five times. The company says it pays about S/259 a day in extortion to the Los Chukis gang and suspects a rival group. More than 200 workers stopped work on 18 November and planned a march to the Interior Ministry.

peru|2026-11-16|ancash huanuco and other.text: 16–18 Nov — Ancash, Huanuco and other regions: Heavy-cargo hauliers held a 72-hour national strike over diesel prices, blocking roads in Casma and other points, with the largest concentration in Huanuco. Organisers claimed about 20,000 participants, though some unions, including Arequipa truckers, stayed out.

peru|2026-11-12|piura lima callao junin|.text: 12–14 Nov — Piura, Lima, Callao, Junin: La Republica reported four people killed in less than 48 hours in separate attacks. The Public Ministry counted 164 attacks on transport workers (93 dead, 124 wounded) from January to 27 October 2026.

bolivia|2026-11-11|el castillo checkpoin.text: 11 Nov — El Castillo checkpoint, Villa Tunari (Chapare): Cocaleros clashed with an anti-drug UMOPAR patrol at dawn. Accounts differ on whether it was an ambush during the anti-drug 'Operation Muralla' or a reaction to police breaking up a vigil. Three officers, including UMOPAR's national commander, were wounded and a police post was burned; police withdrew to Chimore, residents retook the checkpoint, and Morales praised them. No arrests were reported.

bolivia|2026-11-12|la paz cochabamba|pol.text: 12–13 Nov — La Paz/Cochabamba: The government blamed Evo Morales for the El Castillo clash, and police announced reinforcements in the Tropico and prosecutions for the damage. Prosecutors have opened an 'armed uprising' and terrorism investigation in which Morales calls the Government Minister a narco in return.

bolivia|2026-11-13|national|political.text: 13 Nov (reported 16 Nov) — National: At the prosecution's request, the Migration directorate issued an alert barring Morales from leaving Bolivia in the 'armed uprising' case over the 53-day May–June blockade. The case also names COB leader Mario Argollo and Tupac Katari federation leader Vicente Salazar, who is already jailed.

dominican republic|2026-11-12|jimani|mil.text: 12 Nov — Jimani: An EFE report from the border found crossings operating normally under a heavy military presence, with General Soto Thorman saying the frontier is 'secure and under Dominican control'. About 11,000 troops are deployed from Montecristi to Pedernales, reinforced since late October by special-forces battalions, armoured vehicles and drones.

dominican republic|2026-11-16|border|mil.text: 16 Nov — Border: EFE reported the border fence, under construction for five years, gaining renewed priority because of Haiti's gang violence. When complete it will cover 160 km of the 391-km land border. President Abinader has said gangs will not be allowed to establish themselves within 20 km of the frontier.

jamaica|2026-11-11|ellerslie pen spanish.text: 11–12 Nov — Ellerslie Pen, Spanish Town (St Catherine): A police-military team fatally shot 23-year-old security guard Shevon Ulett during a search. Police say he fired at them first.

jamaica|2026-11-14|portmore|armed-attack.text: 14 Nov — Portmore (St Catherine): Police fatally shot a man known as 'Topey' who they say attacked officers with a machete after an earlier dispute. INDECOM has opened a probe.

gaza|2026-11-24|gaza strip|airstrike.text: 24 Nov — Gaza Strip: An Israeli strike killed Naim Abu Nahl, director-general of Hamas's Internal Security Service, according to Hamas and Middle East Eye.

gaza|2026-11-25|gaza city shati camp|air.text: 25 Nov — Gaza City (Shati camp): An overnight Israeli air strike on an apartment killed Muhammad Abu al-Awf, director of internal security in northern Gaza, along with his wife and two daughters aged 13 and 15. It was the second killing of a senior Hamas security official in under 24 hours.

gaza|2026-11-26|deir al balah|airstrike.text: 26 Nov — Deir al-Balah: An overnight Israeli strike on an apartment building killed Hamas deputy education minister Khaled Abu Nada and his wife, according to Palestinian media; the IDF said it targeted a 'senior' Hamas operative.

gaza|2026-11-26|gaza city shati camp|air.text: 26 Nov — Gaza City (Shati camp): Palestinian media reported three people killed in another Israeli strike; Al Jazeera counted at least 16 Palestinians killed across Gaza in 24 hours.

lebanon|2026-11-21|braachit bint jbeil d.text: 21 Nov — Braachit (Bint Jbeil district): An Israeli air strike targeted the town, according to Al Jazeera reporting compiled by the CFR conflict tracker; no casualty figures were given.

lebanon|2026-11-22|majdal zoun qantara|s.text: 22 Nov — Majdal Zoun / Qantara: Lebanese state media reported Israeli shelling of Majdal Zoun and demolitions in Qantara.

lebanon|2026-11-24|qabrikha touline zawt.place: Qabrikha / Touline / Zawtar al-Sharqiyah / Mayfadoun / Kfar Tebnit
lebanon|2026-11-24|qabrikha touline zawt.text: 24 Nov — Qabrikha / Touline / Zawtar al-Sharqiyah / Mayfadoun / Kfar Tebnit: Lebanese media reported a series of Israeli strikes and explosions in the IDF's southern buffer zone, and state media said at least three Israeli drones exploded over southern towns; the IDF calls such activity routine demolition of Hezbollah infrastructure. No casualties were reported.

iran|2026-11-21|bahrain riffa awali isa.text: 21 Nov — Bahrain (Riffa / Awali / Isa / Juffair): Iran launched two waves of drones and ballistic missiles at US-used bases in Bahrain; the IRGC claimed hits on Patriot radars. Bahrain said its air defences intercepted several attacks, but a civilian industrial facility was hit and set on fire, injuring two people. A US official said no US forces were damaged and called it the fourth attempt in about a week.

iran|2026-11-21|sirik hormozgan|other.text: 21 Nov — Sirik (Hormozgan): Explosions and air-defence activity were reported in the southern Iranian town shortly after the Bahrain attacks, according to Iranian accounts; CENTCOM denied an Iranian claim that a surface-to-air missile damaged a US F-16 on 20 Nov.

iran|2026-11-21|strait of hormuz|maritim.text: 21 Nov — Strait of Hormuz: At least three tankers were attacked in or near the strait. UKMTO reported two tankers hit by projectiles as they exited the Gulf, with no casualties, and Iran's navy said a third hit a mine east of the strait and caught fire. Reports put the number of tankers hit since 16 Nov at seven.

iran|2026-11-24|strait of hormuz|maritim.text: 24–25 Nov — Strait of Hormuz: The IRGC said three tankers caught fire after hitting naval mines on 24 Nov, and two more on 25 Nov, while transiting an 'unauthorized route' despite US escorts. UKMTO did not confirm the mine reports. Al Jazeera estimates Hormuz oil traffic is down about 40%.

yemen|2026-11-20|hodeidah sanaa|airstrik.text: 20 Nov — Hodeidah / Sanaa: The Saudi-led coalition carried out a 'special operation' against Houthi smuggling and weapons-transport capabilities at Hodeidah port and struck military targets in Sanaa, including a main supply depot. Houthi media reported a strike on Mokha port.

yemen|2026-11-20|marib al jawf lahij|gro.text: 20 Nov — Marib / al-Jawf / Lahij: Government forces reported six air strikes on Houthi positions north of Marib and clashes in al-Jawf and Lahij; more than 350,000 people have been displaced, with Taiz receiving the most.

yemen|2026-11-23|hodeidah|airstrike.text: 23 Nov — Hodeidah: Houthi media reported 10 people killed in a coalition strike that hit a building of the Public Telecommunications Corporation.

yemen|2026-11-25|hodeidah|airstrike.text: 25 Nov — Hodeidah: After ordering civilians to evacuate Hodeidah port on 24 Nov, the coalition said it struck Houthi 'operational capabilities' at the port, and Houthi media said the city's airport was also hit. The Houthis threatened all Saudi Red Sea ports, and AFP reported Houthi fighters about 60 km from Aden, where defences are being prepared.

israel|2026-11-21|dura al qara near rama.text: 21 Nov — Dura al-Qara (near Ramallah, West Bank): Hamza Masoud Salim Abdo, 42, died of gunfire that a Palestinian official attributed to guards of a nearby settlement, according to the Palestinian Health Ministry; the IDF said it was looking into the incident.

israel|2026-11-23|al rashayida area east.place: al-Rashayida area (east of Bethlehem, West Bank)
israel|2026-11-23|al rashayida area east.text: 23 Nov — al-Rashayida area (east of Bethlehem, West Bank): A Palestinian shepherd was shot dead by a settler, according to official Palestinian sources. The Palestinian civil affairs authority reported about 30 settler attacks in one day, including the torching of some 12 vehicles north of Ramallah.

israel|2026-11-23|tel aviv washington|di.text: 23 Nov — Tel Aviv / Washington: The US reportedly decided to hold off at least a week on new strikes on Iran despite Israeli pressure, with Netanyahu pushing for a short, intense campaign and Mossad chief Gofman lobbying in Washington the week before.

israel|2026-11-25|jerusalem|political.text: 25 Nov — Jerusalem: Eisenkot's Yashar signed a coalition agreement with Yisrael Beytenu (reportedly giving Liberman's party the Defence ministry) and is aiming for a swearing-in as early as 2 Dec; the Democrats froze talks and UTJ is seeking rabbinic approval to open formal negotiations.

iraq|2026-11-20|jurf al sakhar babil|mil.text: 19–20 Nov — Jurf al-Sakhar (Babil): After a compromise reached on 19 Nov, Iraqi security forces arrived on 20 Nov. Federal Police are to run a new control headquarters, Energy Police are securing the oil pipeline, and an army brigade, a Federal Police battalion and two PMF brigades will guard pipelines. Kataib Hezbollah is expected to withdraw within a month; PM al-Zaidi said the forces were 'not waging war'.

iraq|2026-11-25|jurf al sakhar babil|mil.text: 25 Nov — Jurf al-Sakhar (Babil): Al-Mada, cited by 964media, reported that Kataib Hezbollah still controls the centre of the town and that no government force has entered it, contradicting earlier reports of a full deployment.

iraq|2026-11-25|baghdad|political.text: 25 Nov — Baghdad: Iraq's Federal Supreme Court ruled that Baghdad may deploy federal troops to secure international borders, including in territory administered by the Kurdistan Region; the KRG rejected the orders as unconstitutional.

iraq|2026-11-25|al luhais south of baghd.text: 25 Nov — Al Luhais (south of Baghdad): The National Security Service reported two more oil-smuggling operations, including a tapped pipeline, as the government widened its crackdown on illicit oil networks.

saudi arabia|2026-11-19|riyadh king abdu.text: 19 Nov — Riyadh (King Abdullah Financial District): A Houthi missile hit the Public Investment Fund tower, blowing out windows across seven to eight floors; Saudi civil defence reported material damage to the tower and nearby buildings and no injuries.

saudi arabia|2026-11-21|riyadh|missile-s.text: 21 Nov — Riyadh: The coalition intercepted three Houthi ballistic missiles fired at the capital after eight emergency alerts in 24 hours, the third consecutive day of alerts; a drone aimed at the kingdom's south was destroyed hours later.

saudi arabia|2026-11-25|riyadh western r.text: 25 Nov — Riyadh / Western Region: The coalition said it intercepted two ballistic missiles fired at Riyadh and a cruise missile aimed at the Western Region; the Houthis said they targeted Jeddah and Jazan ports in response to strikes on Hodeidah and threatened all Saudi Red Sea ports.

saudi arabia|2026-11-26|jeddah riyadh|dr.text: 26 Nov — Jeddah / Riyadh: Saudi air defences destroyed a drone near Jeddah Islamic Port overnight, and an explosion was heard over Riyadh around midnight as missiles were downed; coalition spokesman al-Maliki said no civilians were injured by debris.

syria|2026-11-24|jubata al khashab north.text: 24 Nov — Jubata al-Khashab (northern Quneitra): Israeli troops detained a Syrian civilian during a raid, according to Alikhbaria TV; he was released the next day.

syria|2026-11-24|ain al bayda quneitra|m.text: 24 Nov — Ain al-Bayda (Quneitra): Israeli forces entered the village and set up a checkpoint to search passersby, according to Syrian state media.

syria|2026-11-24|abidin daraa|military-a.text: 24 Nov — Abidin (Daraa): An Israeli force with seven military vehicles entered the village and searched several homes, according to Anadolu citing Syrian media.

syria|2026-11-25|quneitra countryside|sh.text: 25 Nov (reported) — Quneitra countryside: Israeli forces destroyed farmland and a livestock shelter and blocked farmers from their land, and state media reported Israeli shelling of farmland near al-Mantara Dam, with no casualties.

egypt|2026-11-23|cairo doha ankara|diplo.text: 23 Nov — Cairo / Doha / Ankara: Egypt was reported alongside Qatar, Turkey, Saudi Arabia and Pakistan as working to restart US–Iran talks, as Washington weighed delaying new strikes on Iran.

egypt|2026-11-25|cairo|humanitarian.text: 25 Nov — Cairo: The Foreign Ministry said it is following up on missing Egyptian nationals after a migrant boat carrying 27 Egyptians sank off Benghazi, Libya (the sinking occurred on 5 Nov).

libya|2026-11-22|benghazi port|maritime.text: 22 Nov — Benghazi (port): Ukrainian naval drones sank the Russian Black Sea Fleet corvette Merkury (Project 20380) in the port, also striking the cargo ship MV Angara and reportedly destroying a Ka-27 helicopter. Zelenskyy said seven naval drones were used, and Reuters, citing local medical sources, reported about 10 injured, including Russians and Libyans.

libya|2026-11-23|tripoli benghazi|politi.text: 23–24 Nov — Tripoli / Benghazi: The Presidential Council vowed military, political and legal measures over the Benghazi incidents, Libya demanded clarification from Kyiv and considered an international lawsuit against Ukraine, and the African Union condemned the attacks on the port.

libya|2026-11-23|tripoli|political.text: 23 Nov — Tripoli: Presidential Council head Menfi met the 5+5 Joint Military Commission on military unification; the Ports Authority warned that maritime security threats could disrupt supplies.

libya|2026-11-25|ankara|diplomatic.text: 25 Nov — Ankara: Turkish President Erdogan received Khalifa Haftar on his first official visit to Turkey, as the US reaffirmed support for a Libyan-led, consensus-based political process.

tunisia|2026-11-20|tunis|political.text: 20 Nov — Tunis: A court sentenced Sihem Bensedrine, 76, former head of the Truth and Dignity Commission, to five years in prison on corruption charges; ex-commission member Khaled Krichi received four years and ex-minister Mabrouk Korchid six. Amnesty International called the verdict an 'outrageous injustice'.

ukraine|2026-11-20|kyiv|missile-strike.text: 20 Nov — Kyiv: In what Moscow called retaliation for the Kerch Bridge strike, Russia fired more than 400 drones and more than 110 missiles, 27 of them ballistic, at energy, transport and rail targets, per Zelensky. The Podilskyi, Darnytskyi and Southern bridges were damaged and traffic restricted. At least eight people were killed (six in Kyiv, including three water-facility workers, and two in Lviv) and 28 wounded, per Prime Minister Koretskyi. A hospital in Zaporizhzhia Oblast was also hit, and nuclear plants cut output, causing outages in Kyiv and 10 regions (Al Jazeera).

ukraine|2026-11-20|kryvyi rih|missile-st.text: 20 Nov — Kryvyi Rih: In a Russian 'triple-tap' strike, local officials said ballistic missiles hit a restaurant parking lot and drones then struck rescuers at the scene. A seven-year-old boy and a 20-year-old paramedic were killed (CNN).

ukraine|2026-11-25|kharkiv zaporizhzhia.text: 24–25 Nov — Kharkiv, Zaporizhzhia and Kyiv oblasts: ISW recorded no advances by either side on 24 November and counted 96 Russian drones overnight, 64 of them jet-powered. Overnight into 25 November Russia launched 112 strike drones, of which 88 were neutralised. A drone hit a minibus near Fedorivka in Kharkiv Oblast, killing one and injuring seven, one man was killed in Bila Tserkva district, and much of Zaporizhzhia city and oblast lost power (Ukrainska Pravda, via a Substack digest).

ukraine|2026-11-24|kyiv|diplomatic.text: 24 Nov — Kyiv: Zelensky told Bloomberg that US envoys Witkoff and Kushner want a peace deal 'as soon as possible', ideally by January, but that peace must not come 'at Ukraine's expense alone'. Trump said on 25 November he is 'not under a timeline' (Ukrainska Pravda, Meduza). The Abu Dhabi prisoner exchange had still not been reported as carried out.

russia|2026-11-19|almetyevsk tatarstan|d.text: 19 Nov — Almetyevsk (Tatarstan): Ukrainian drones attacked oil storage tanks near Almetyevsk. The Tatarstan head's press service confirmed the attack and said a major fire was avoided, while Astra reported the Transneft Kaleikino pumping station, a Druzhba pipeline hub, as the target (Meduza).
