russia|2026-11-20|smolensk oblast|drone-.text: 20 Nov — Smolensk Oblast: A Ukrainian drone attack damaged an industrial facility, and Russia's Defence Ministry said it intercepted 310 Ukrainian drones. The same night, Russian strikes sent two likely missiles and a drone into Polish airspace, which Poland's defence minister called a provocation (Al Jazeera). Russia's embassy in Warsaw later called Polish protests 'Russophobic'.

russia|2026-11-23|murmansk|political.text: 23 Nov — Murmansk: Law enforcement arrested Murmansk Oblast Governor Andrei Chibis, which ISW calls the first arrest of a sitting Russian governor since the full-scale invasion. ISW also reports Putin acknowledging that Ukraine's strikes on oil infrastructure impose a substantial financial burden on the budget.

russia|2026-11-25|samara oblast|drone-st.text: 25 Nov — Samara Oblast: Fires broke out overnight at Rosneft's Novokuibyshevsk and Syzran refineries after a drone attack, per Astra and Ukrainska Pravda, but there was no official confirmation that the plants were hit.

belarus|2026-11-24|minsk|diplomatic.text: 24 Nov — Minsk: In an interview with Le Point published on 24 November, Lukashenko proposed that he and Zelensky fly together to Moscow for talks to end the war, offering himself as a guarantor of Zelensky's safety. He said Russian forces were winning 'slowly' and that Russia, Ukraine and Belarus should decide the region's arrangements (Reuters via Belta). Zelensky has rejected going to Moscow and instead invited Lukashenko and Putin to Kyiv.

belarus|2026-11-25|minsk|political.text: 25 Nov — Minsk: In the same interview, Lukashenko said Belarus would consider removing Russian nuclear weapons from its territory as part of a Ukraine peace settlement, denied knowing in 2022 that Russian troops in Belarus would attack Kyiv, and ruled out his son Nikolai succeeding him (Ukrainska Pravda).

moldova|2026-11-19|chis ina u|political.text: 19 Nov — Chișinău: Parliament ratified, with 56 votes, a five-year military-technical cooperation agreement with Ukraine signed on 26 October, covering expertise sharing, training, technology transfer and joint defence capability (Moldova1).

moldova|2026-11-20|s tefan voda district.text: 20 Nov — Ștefan Vodă district: A drone entered Moldovan airspace at 14:48 from Ukraine's Odesa region toward Crocmaz and left a minute later near Tudora, per the Defence Ministry. Separately, a drone crossed from Ukraine near Arioneşti in Dondușeni district and exited about nine minutes later through Briceni district (Moldova Live).

moldova|2026-11-23|northern and eastern.text: 21–23 Nov — Northern and eastern Moldova: A jet-powered drone crossed Moldovan airspace twice on 21 November, and on 23 November an unidentified drone, likely Russian, entered and was lost near the eastern border, likely after returning to Ukraine (Moldova1, ISW). The General Staff counted 19 incursions in November and said Moldova can detect drones but lacks the means to neutralise them.

georgia|2026-11-22|tbilisi|political.text: 22–23 Nov — Tbilisi: President Kavelashvili pardoned 232 convicts on St George's Day, but only three were political prisoners: Giorgi Mindadze, Anri Kvaratskhelia and Nikoloz Javakhishvili. Activist Giorgi Okmelashvili, jailed over the 2024 foreign-agents protests, was also freed (Caucasian Knot).

georgia|2026-11-23|tbilisi|unrest.text: 23 Nov — Tbilisi: Pro-European protests outside parliament and the city assembly reached their 726th day, with at least 200 people demanding new elections, the release of political prisoners and the repeal of repressive laws. Organisers are building toward the 28 November anniversary rally (Caucasian Knot).

georgia|2026-11-25|batumi|political.text: 25 Nov — Batumi: At the Constitutional Court hearing on Georgian Dream's lawsuit to ban five opposition parties, Chairman Nadaraia again ordered Coalition for Change leader Nika Gvaramia out of the courtroom. The hearing was postponed to 30 November after a judge's father died (JAMnews).

georgia|2026-11-25|brussels tbilisi|dipl.text: 25 Nov — Brussels/Tbilisi: The European Commission proposed removing Georgia's Kulevi oil refinery from the Russia sanctions list, which PM Kobakhidze welcomed. The same day, UNM member Anatoli Gigauri was released after serving two years on protest-related charges (JAMnews).

armenia|2026-11-23|yerevan|political.text: 23 Nov — Yerevan: Pashinyan published the draft of Armenia's new constitution, said it would secure peace, and vowed to resign if voters reject it (Public Radio of Armenia). Opposition factions, including the Armenia Alliance, said they would not provide the votes needed to send the draft to a referendum, for which Civil Contract lacks a two-thirds majority (Armenpress).

armenia|2026-11-23|syunik washington|dip.text: 23 Nov — Syunik/Washington: Pashinyan and Trump announced the launch of the practical phase of the Trump Route for International Peace and Prosperity (TRIPP) linking mainland Azerbaijan with Nakhchivan through Syunik. Deputy Foreign Minister Kostanyan said on 25 November that rail construction would start in 2027, and Iranian adviser Mokhber warned against routes bypassing Iran (Armenian Weekly, JAMnews).

armenia|2026-11-25|yerevan moscow|diplom.text: 25–26 Nov — Yerevan/Moscow: Deputy PM Mher Grigoryan held talks with Russian Deputy PM Overchuk in Moscow, and the Kremlin said it is preparing for Pashinyan's 3 December working visit. Moscow wants him to say whether he will attend the 22 December CIS summit in St Petersburg (Public Radio of Armenia, JAMnews).

azerbaijan|2026-11-19|baku|political.text: 19 Nov — Baku: Human rights defender Bashir Suleymanli was sentenced to 7.5 years in prison, and Human Rights Watch called for his release (JAMnews).

azerbaijan|2026-11-24|baku|political.text: 24–25 Nov — Baku: In the closed trial of Popular Front leader Ali Karimli and deputy Mammad Ibrahim on charges of attempting to seize power by force, relatives of former presidential administration head Ramiz Mehdiyev testified on 24 November and the hearing was adjourned for further witnesses. Both defendants deny the charges (1news.az, JAMnews).

azerbaijan|2026-11-24|ig dır tu rkiye|di.text: 24–25 Nov — Iğdır (Türkiye): Aliyev and Erdoğan backed the 'Zangezur corridor' at the International Caucasus Congress. Foreign Minister Bayramov said Baku hopes TRIPP will be implemented soon, and Aliyev said over 100,000 tonnes of cargo had transited Azerbaijan to Armenia over the past year (Armenian Weekly, JAMnews).

mali|2026-11-21|niono se gou region|arme.text: 21 Nov — Niono, Ségou region: JNIM attacked several army and Russian Africa Corps positions, including the town's main military installations. Gunfire and heavy-weapon explosions hit the referral health centre, killing one health worker; MSF treated 26 wounded. RFI reported about thirty dead in total, including one civilian; the army disputes JNIM's claimed toll.

mali|2026-11-20|tinzaouate ne kidal regi.text: Night of 20–21 Nov — Tinzaouatène, Kidal region: The army general staff said a strike on an ammunition depot 'neutralised' 23 fighters and destroyed the stock and a pick-up, and a second strike destroyed an illegal gold-processing site. Not independently verified.

mali|2026-11-22|talhandak and tinzaouate.text: Night of 22–23 Nov — Talhandak and Tinzaouatène, Kidal region: The army said strikes destroyed a depot with more than 90 motorcycles and spare parts at Talhandak and killed 11 fighters at Tinzaouatène; on 23 Nov it also struck armed men and two trucks near Farabougou (Ségou). Army figures only.

mali|2026-11-23|north east of niono and.place: North-east of Niono and other areas
mali|2026-11-23|north east of niono and.text: 23–24 Nov — North-east of Niono and other areas: The army said strikes linked to the hunt for the Niono attackers killed about ten fighters and destroyed seven motorcycles, according to APA. Not independently verified.

niger|2026-11-24|near baroua diffa regio.text: 24 Nov — Near Baroua, Diffa region: Boko Haram fighters attacked an army patrol, killing 11 soldiers and wounding five, according to a provisional defence ministry toll reported by AFP. The ministry said 22 attackers were 'neutralised'.

niger|2026-11-21|between tillabe ri and.text: 21–22 Nov — Between Tillabéri and Niamey: A Saudi national was reportedly kidnapped by fighters suspected of belonging to IS Sahel, two security sources told Reuters. No group has claimed it and the authorities have not commented.

niger|2026-11-24|niamey|political.text: 24–25 Nov — Niamey: Gen. Tiani opened the first 'Invest in Niger' forum and received the trade ministers of Burkina Faso and Mali, underlining AES economic integration amid the junta's isolation since the August mutiny.

burkina faso|2026-11-22|selmagui kaya ar.text: 22 Nov — Selmagui, Kaya area (Centre-North): JNIM claimed it took control of a position of state-backed VDP militia in the evening, according to claims relayed by the Sahel Alerte monitoring account. No toll was given and the claim cannot be independently verified.

burkina faso|2026-11-25|burkina faso mal.text: 25 Nov — Burkina Faso, Mali and Niger: A Reuters review of ACLED data found JNIM had carried out 187 drone attacks between 2023 and mid-November 2026 (235 including the FLA). JNIM has used them against army positions such as Djibo in Burkina Faso.

sudan|2026-11-24|ed damazin blue nile|dr.text: 24 Nov — Ed Damazin, Blue Nile: Drone strikes on three residential neighbourhoods killed at least 19 civilians from three families and wounded 15, according to the rights group Emergency Lawyers, which blamed the RSF (Reuters). Sudan Tribune, citing a local civil-society group, gave at least 14 dead. The RSF did not comment.

sudan|2026-11-24|roseires blue nile|dron.text: 24 Nov — Roseires, Blue Nile: Earlier the same day, drones targeted the Roseires dam and power facilities, wounding five civilians. Emergency Lawyers warned of possible disruption to Blue Nile's electricity and the national grid.

sudan|2026-11-20|around al nahud and abu.place: Around Al-Nahud and Abu Zabad, West Kordofan
sudan|2026-11-20|around al nahud and abu.text: 20 Nov — Around Al-Nahud and Abu Zabad, West Kordofan: The army said it had dismantled RSF defences in 10 areas during a week-long offensive, after seizing five localities around Al-Sa'atat on 16 Nov; the Joint Force said it retook eight areas. The RSF still holds Al-Nahud.

sudan|2026-11-19|nyala south darfur|airs.text: 19 Nov — Nyala, South Darfur: Army aircraft struck what Sudan Tribune described as RSF headquarters after drones circled the city for more than 45 minutes. Residents heard three loud explosions in northern and eastern Nyala, and fighters including an officer were reportedly killed or wounded.

chad|2026-11-19|tibesti|ground-clash.text: 19 Nov — Tibesti: RFI reported that fighting between the army and the Miski Self-Defence Committee continues. Signatories of the April 2025 Miski accord, including the MADAT rebel movement, accuse the government of not honouring it and cite air strikes and a blockade. N'Djamena calls its campaign a law-and-order operation and says dialogue channels remain open.

chad|2026-11-21|abe che ouaddai|military.text: 21 Nov — Abéché, Ouaddaï: The Coordination of the Eastern Operational Zones displayed 450 weapons, about 15,250 rounds of ammunition and 201 magazines seized in Adré, Birak, Haraz, Tissi and on Abéché patrols, reflecting the flow of arms along the Sudan border.

mauritania|2026-11-23|off nouadhibou|mar.text: 23 Nov — Off Nouadhibou: The navy rescued a boat carrying 93 migrants (69 men, 17 women, seven minors) bound for the Canary Islands, the army said. A week earlier coast guards intercepted a canoe from Bargny, Senegal, carrying 179 people.

nigeria|2026-11-21|lumma ba are borgu lg.place: Lumma Ba'are, Borgu LGA, Niger State
nigeria|2026-11-21|lumma ba are borgu lg.text: 21 Nov — Lumma Ba'are, Borgu LGA, Niger State: Attackers killed five people, including the village head, injured five and burned houses, according to the state information commissioner (AP). Residents assumed the attackers were Fulani; local media reported one arrest.

nigeria|2026-11-22|fulani communities in.place: Fulani communities in Borgu LGA, Niger State
nigeria|2026-11-22|fulani communities in.text: 22–24 Nov — Fulani communities in Borgu LGA, Niger State: Reprisal raids, reportedly by more than 300 people from Lumma Ba'are, followed. MACBAN said 64 people from Fulani communities were killed over the weekend, and residents told Reuters at least 30 were killed and homes burned on 24 Nov. Amnesty International said it had videos of children being killed. There is no official toll.

nigeria|2026-11-22|qua an pan lga platea.text: 22 Nov — Qua'an Pan LGA, Plateau: Gunmen attacked a herding community, reportedly killing at least four herders and rustling more than 100 cattle (Parrot Nigeria). A curfew was imposed in Qua'an Pan the next evening after further violence, and houses were razed in Bong, Doemak district.

nigeria|2026-11-23|tumbuna abadam lga bo.text: 23 Nov — Tumbuna, Abadam LGA, Borno: Two air strikes at about 1 a.m. reportedly killed eight ISWAP fighters, according to military-sourced reports. Not independently verified.

north korea|2026-11-26|undisclosed sites.text: 26 Nov — Undisclosed sites: KCNA said Kim Jong Un inspected nuclear-material production and weapons research facilities. He called for tactical nuclear weapons to be deployed 'across multiple domains for different missions', said the country's nuclear status 'will never change' and warned that denying it would be 'an open declaration of war'. Bloomberg noted a rare display of warheads (Reuters, AP, Al Jazeera).

north korea|2026-11-19|yongbyon|military.text: 19 Nov — Yongbyon: The IAEA said North Korea is expanding a uranium enrichment facility (Al Jazeera). On 25 Nov NK News reported imagery suggesting the North tested an ICBM engine while Trump was seeking a meeting.

north korea|2026-11-24|pyongyang|diploma.text: 24–25 Nov — Pyongyang: North Korea condemned Swiss sanctions on the Songdowon children's camp, which is allegedly linked to transfers of children from occupied Ukraine. It declared Swiss office head Sylvain Astier persona non grata with 48 hours to leave and forced the office, reopened in late October, to close (Al Jazeera, Reuters).

north korea|2026-11-22|pyongyang|diploma.text: 22–23 Nov — Pyongyang: For the first time, Kim personally accepted credentials from new ambassadors, including those of India and the Philippines, and vowed to expand ties with 'friendly' states (NK News, WSJ, Inquirer). No ballistic missile launch was reported in the window.

myanmar|2026-11-19|the hague|diplomatic.text: 19 Nov — The Hague: The ICJ ruled in The Gambia v. Myanmar that Myanmar committed genocide against the Rohingya in 2017, the first time the court has found a state responsible for genocide. The junta rejected the ruling as unfair. On 24 Nov the UK sanctioned five military officers and announced a ban on aviation-fuel supplies (UN News, AP, Myanmar Now).

myanmar|2026-11-21|pauktaw township rakh.text: 21–22 Nov — Pauktaw Township, Rakhine: Junta jets bombed Thawin Chaung and Nan Tet Kyun villages over the weekend, killing four civilians, including a five-month-old infant, and injuring 13, according to locals (Myanmar Now; Narinjara reported the strike under the AA name Wirathani).

myanmar|2026-11-22|ponnagyun township ra.text: 22–24 Nov — Ponnagyun Township, Rakhine: The AA said junta airstrikes on two villages killed two civilians, including a cattle herder, and injured one (Narinjara).

myanmar|2026-11-22|kyaukphyu and ngapyi.text: 22 Nov — Kyaukphyu and Ngapyi Island, Rakhine: Narinjara reported intensified fighting around Kyaukphyu and said about 20 regime soldiers had been killed on Ngapyi Island in recent days. This is unverified and comes from an AA-aligned outlet.

pakistan|2026-11-21|mastung balochistan|.text: 21 Nov — Mastung, Balochistan: Security forces said they killed 15 militants they called 'Fitna al-Hindustan' (Baloch separatists) in two operations under Radd-ul-Fitna-III, praised by PM Shehbaz Sharif and the Balochistan chief minister. On 26 Nov ISPR reported 12 more killed in Balochistan operations (Express Tribune, Aaj, Geo).

pakistan|2026-11-22|balochistan|drone-st.text: 22–24 Nov — Balochistan: The BLA claimed it killed 20 Pakistani personnel in a series of attacks across the province, including armed-drone strikes, and Indian outlets reported a BLA attack that killed five FC personnel. Pakistan has not confirmed these claims and they are unverified (Hans India, News18).

pakistan|2026-11-24|peshawar kohat and b.place: Peshawar, Kohat and Bannu, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa
pakistan|2026-11-24|peshawar kohat and b.text: 21–24 Nov — Peshawar, Kohat and Bannu, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa: A joint CTD–army raid killed three TTP militants on Peshawar's outskirts, and police killed three in Kohat. On 24 Nov the CTD killed five TTP militants in a Peshawar raid while a TTP commander escaped, and Operation Sarbulandi killed three more in Bannu (Arab News PK, Dunya, Bol News).

pakistan|2026-11-22|pakistan afghanistan.text: 22 Nov — Pakistan–Afghanistan border: Islamabad warned the Taliban over alleged cross-border drone activity, and Kabul accused Pakistan of backing anti-Taliban armed groups. Pakistan excluded Afghanistan from a regional conference, and no ceasefire or border reopening was reported (Kabul Tribune, Arab News PK, Afghanistan International).

india|2026-11-20|imphal west manipur|gro.text: 20 Nov — Imphal West, Manipur: Security forces killed a suspected KCP militant, reported to be an ex-serviceman, in a gunfight and arrested eight others, including a surrendered KCP-PWG chairman (The Hindu, NDTV, India Today NE).

india|2026-11-22|manipur|political.text: 22 Nov — Manipur: The families of the four victims of the October Nongshum ambush accepted the bodies after a month-long protest, once the government agreed to an 11-point charter of demands (Assam Tribune, Rediff). No new mass-casualty attack was found after the 13 Nov Ukhrul killings.

india|2026-11-21|jammu and kashmir|polit.text: 21–23 Nov — Jammu and Kashmir: Home Minister Amit Shah said 'not a single local terrorist' remains in the Kashmir Valley after the killing of LeT commander Lateef Bhat. Security officials say about 65 Pakistani militants are on their radar and claim the ISI is planning fresh attacks (Open, Mid-Day, Republic).

china|2026-11-19|shenzhen|diplomatic.text: 19 Nov — Shenzhen: At their bilateral talks Xi told Trump the US must do 'the right thing' on Taiwan to avoid 'great turbulence'. Xinhua said Trump stated the US 'does not support Taiwan independence', which the White House had not confirmed. The Xi–Trump–Putin trilateral issued a statement on UN reform, energy security and non-proliferation, without addressing Taiwan or Ukraine (RFA, SCMP, GMA/AP).

china|2026-11-19|antelope reef paracel i.text: 19 Nov — Antelope Reef, Paracel Islands: Analysts cited by AFP said a runway of nearly 3 km is being built on China's newly reclaimed island at Antelope Reef. It would be Beijing's second runway in the Paracels and part of the first major island-building since 2017 (Jiji, Kuwait Times).

china|2026-11-22|around taiwan|military-.text: 21–22 Nov — Around Taiwan: After the summit, PLA activity reported by Taiwan's MND rose from two aircraft in the 21 Nov report to 24 aircraft, 12 ships and two balloons in the 22 Nov report, with 10 balloons detected over three days before Taiwan's 28 Nov local elections (Taiwan News, Taipei Times).

china|2026-11-25|south china sea|militar.text: 25 Nov — South China Sea: The Philippine military confirmed that a PLA H-6 bomber flew over the West Philippine Sea near the Philippine coast, as the AFP counted 48 Chinese coast guard and navy vessels in Philippine-claimed waters in the week after the ASEAN summit (Philstar, Manila Times, ABS-CBN).

taiwan|2026-11-19|shenzhen|political.text: 19 Nov — Shenzhen: Xi warned Trump that the US must do 'the right thing' on Taiwan to avoid 'great turbulence', and Xinhua reported Trump saying the US does not support Taiwan independence, which the White House had not confirmed (RFA, GMA/AP).

taiwan|2026-11-19|taiwan adiz|military-a.text: 19 Nov — Taiwan ADIZ: The MND reported two Russian Tu-95 bombers entering Taiwan's ADIZ on their return from Vietnam, the second Russian approach that week, and Taiwan and Japan scrambled jets (Reuters via WMBD, The Aviationist).

taiwan|2026-11-22|around taiwan|military.text: 21–22 Nov — Around Taiwan: The MND tracked 24 PLA aircraft, 12 ships and two balloons in the 24 hours to 22 Nov, up from two aircraft the day before, and detected 10 Chinese balloons over three days in the run-up to the 28 Nov local elections (Taiwan News, Taipei Times).

taiwan|2026-11-26|around taiwan|military.text: 26 Nov — Around Taiwan: Two days before the local elections, the MND tracked six PLA naval ships and two military aircraft (Taiwan News).

philippines|2026-11-24|off panata island.text: 24 Nov — Off Panata Island, Spratlys: The PCG said a Chinese maritime militia vessel made dangerous manoeuvres against BRP Cabra and its RHIB and nearly collided with them, while the PCG ordered out two militia vessels anchored in Philippine territorial waters (PNA, Manila Bulletin, ABS-CBN).

philippines|ongoing|west philippine sea|.text: 17–23 Nov — West Philippine Sea: The AFP said Chinese coast guard and navy vessels in the West Philippine Sea rose to 48 in the week after the ASEAN summit (ABS-CBN, Inquirer).

philippines|2026-11-25|west philippine s.text: 25 Nov — West Philippine Sea: The AFP confirmed that a Chinese H-6 bomber flew over the West Philippine Sea near the Philippine coast (Philstar, Manila Times).

philippines|2026-11-23|kidapawan city co.text: 23 Nov — Kidapawan City, Cotabato: The police chief of Bubong, Lanao del Sur, was shot dead inside a boarding house. The PNP ordered a manhunt and named four suspects (Inquirer, Philstar).

south korea|2026-11-24|ulleungdo east se.text: 24 Nov — Ulleungdo, East Sea: Russian warplanes, reported as Tu-160 bombers, entered the KADIZ and came within about 24 km of Ulleungdo, prompting fighter scrambles and a first-ever preemptive air-raid alert on the island. The JCS said there was no airspace violation, and the foreign ministry expressed regret to Moscow (Yonhap, Korea JoongAng Daily, Chosun Ilbo).

south korea|2026-11-23|seoul|political.text: 23 Nov — Seoul: President Lee nominated new foreign and unification ministers and a new intelligence chief, a shake-up linked to strained intelligence ties with Washington and the deadlock with Pyongyang (NK News, Bloomberg, Straits Times).

vietnam|2026-11-19|da nang|military-acti.text: 19 Nov — Da Nang: Two Russian Tu-95MS bombers, which had landed at Da Nang on 17 Nov with Il-78 tankers, left Vietnam and were intercepted by Japan and Taiwan on the way home. Analysts flagged the use of a civilian airport for strategic aviation (Washington Post, The Aviationist, EurAsian Times).

vietnam|2026-11-19|antelope reef paracel.text: 19 Nov — Antelope Reef, Paracel Islands: Analysts cited by AFP said China is building a runway of nearly 3 km on its new artificial island at Antelope Reef in the Vietnam-claimed Paracels (Jiji, Kuwait Times). On 25 Nov RFA reported that China is pushing its claims through 'patriotic cruises' to the Paracels.

vietnam|2026-11-22|gulf of tonkin|milita.text: 22 Nov — Gulf of Tonkin: The Chinese and Vietnamese navies completed a joint patrol, with PLA anti-submarine ships taking part (SCMP).

vietnam|2026-11-24|japan vietnam|diploma.text: 24 Nov — Japan–Vietnam: The two governments discussed joint production of defence equipment (Indo-Pacific Defense Forum).

japan|2026-11-19|shenzhen|diplomatic.text: 19 Nov — Shenzhen: PM Takaichi met Putin at APEC two days after Japan said two suspected Russian aircraft violated its airspace near Okinoshima for about three minutes. She also said she wants 'constructive and stable' ties with China, but Japanese commentators described her as snubbed by Beijing at the summit (The Diplomat, CNA, JAPAN Forward).

japan|2026-11-19|sea of japan east china.place: Sea of Japan / East China Sea
japan|2026-11-19|sea of japan east china.text: 19 Nov — Sea of Japan / East China Sea: ASDF fighters scrambled to intercept two Russian Tu-95 bombers flying back from Vietnam (Defence Blog, The Aviationist).

japan|2026-11-23|tokyo|political.text: 23 Nov — Tokyo: The government moved to strengthen the coast guard with more patrol boats and drones to counter China (Nikkei Asia).

japan|2026-11-26|senkaku islands|maritim.text: 26 Nov — Senkaku Islands: Japan warned Chinese ships to leave the waters near the disputed islands (AFP via ABS-CBN).

indonesia|2026-11-20|nduga highland papu.text: 20 Nov — Nduga, Highland Papua: The TNI said three TPNPB members, described as leading figures, were killed in a firefight with Rajawali and combat reconnaissance troops (ANTARA, Okezone).

indonesia|2026-11-23|beoga and ilaga pun.text: 22–23 Nov — Beoga and Ilaga, Puncak: Gunmen attributed to the TPNPB shot dead a junior high school teacher in Beoga, and Brimob personnel came under fire while evacuating residents by truck. Hundreds of residents fled to Ilaga after firefights (Tribratanews, detik, Tribun Papua).

indonesia|2026-11-23|jakarta|political.text: 23 Nov — Jakarta: The government designated the Papuan separatists an 'Armed Extremist Group' (KEB) in place of the 'KKB' label. Reports cite 172 people killed in attacks by the group in 2025–26 (ANTARA, iNews).

indonesia|2026-11-25|asmat yahukimo wate.text: 25 Nov — Asmat–Yahukimo waters: The TPNPB's Yahukimo command fired on two boats carrying 12 tonnes of rice to Dekai, wounding one person and leaving another missing, and the boats were reportedly burned. A joint team is searching for the victims (detik, ANTARA, Media Indonesia).

thailand|2026-11-20|narathiwat|other.text: 19–20 Nov — Narathiwat: In a coordinated overnight wave, suspected insurgents attacked CCTV cameras at multiple sites, continuing the pattern of sabotage against the security-camera network (Thai PBS World).

thailand|2026-11-20|bana mueang pattani|.text: 19–20 Nov — Bana, Mueang Pattani: Gunmen ambushed the mayor of Bana outside his home and wounded him (Bangkok Post).

bangladesh|2026-11-20|dhaka|unrest.text: 20 Nov — Dhaka: Arsonists targeted the residence of Minister Humayun Kabir. The Business Standard counted four deaths and arson and bomb attacks in 21 districts over six days, and the government deployed 90 additional BGB platoons nationwide (Firstpost, TBS, Al Jazeera).

bangladesh|2026-11-21|narail|unrest.text: 20–21 Nov — Narail: After the killing of two BNP leaders, more than 50 houses of Awami League supporters, including Hindu homes, were set on fire in reprisal, which sparked further clashes (India Today, Indian Express, Al Jazeera).

bangladesh|2026-11-24|dhaka|political.text: 23–24 Nov — Dhaka: Blasts and arson hit the capital as the government vowed to arrest Hasina if she returns from India. On 24 Nov Hasina said she will return on 16 Dec (Victory Day) and asked for a Biman flight from Delhi (Reuters, BBC, Al Jazeera, NewsDrum).

bangladesh|2026-11-25|gazipur and munshi.text: 24–26 Nov — Gazipur and Munshiganj: Police fired tear gas and sound grenades at garment workers blocking roads over a Tk 17,000 minimum-wage demand (Reuters, NDTV). An Awami League leader was shot dead on 25 Nov (IANS), and a BNP factional clash with gunfire and crude bombs killed one person in Munshiganj on 26 Nov (TBS).

sri lanka|2026-11-20|ahungalla galle dis.text: 20 Nov — Ahungalla, Galle district: Police appealed for public help to arrest a shooting suspect (Daily Mirror).

sri lanka|2026-11-25|colombo|diplomatic.text: 25 Nov — Colombo: China signed an agreement to help modernise Sri Lanka Police, as Tamil groups raised complaints of police abuse (Newswire, Tamil Guardian).

sri lanka|2026-11-26|sri lanka|other.text: 26 Nov — Sri Lanka: A police officer wanted over the theft of a T-56 rifle was arrested in Dubai and returned to Sri Lanka (Ada Derana, The Morning).

venezuela|2026-11-24|caracas|unrest.text: 24 Nov — Caracas: Health, education and university unions marched from La Hoyada toward Miraflores over wages and Christmas bonuses, as part of a 24–48-hour national protest strike. Bolivarian National Police (PNB) cordons stopped the march near Avenida Baralt (Salas and Balconcito corners); marchers reported shoving, beatings and confiscated phones, and between five and ten workers hurt. The injury count comes from one left-wing outlet and is unverified.

venezuela|2026-11-25|caracas ucv aula ma.text: 25 Nov — Caracas (UCV Aula Magna): Maria Corina Machado addressed about 3,000 students at the Central University of Venezuela without hindrance. She promised a transition 'without revenge', called for presidential elections next year and presented her 'Liberal Democratic Republic' platform; she remains excluded from the government–opposition talks.

venezuela|2026-11-19|caracas|political.text: 19–20 Nov — Caracas: The National Assembly's Judicial Nominations Committee closed the call for renewal of the Supreme Court (TSJ) with 1,343 applications; the candidate list was due on 20 November, followed by a 15-working-day objection period. This is the first concrete step on the talks' TSJ agenda item.

venezuela|2026-11-19|miranda fuerte guai.text: 19 Nov — Miranda (Fuerte Guaicaipuro): The Venezuelan Prison Observatory said about 70 detainees at the Guaicaipuro military detention centre are held in roofless areas without electricity, exposed to sun and rain. Foro Penal's latest count remains 321 political prisoners, 140 of them military.

colombia|2026-11-21|dagua valle del cauc.text: 21 Nov — Dagua, Valle del Cauca (vereda La Elsa): President De la Espriella announced 'Operation Neptuno', an aerial bombing of the ELN's Luis Carlos Cardenas Arbelaez front (led by alias 'Berta') that killed five alleged members. He called it the 10th strategic bombing of his government; one EFE report places the strike earlier in the week.

colombia|2026-11-21|mapiripan meta|airst.text: 21 Nov — Mapiripan, Meta: A pre-dawn bombing, 'Operation Ninfa', against Front 44 'Antonio Ricaurte' of Ivan Mordisco's FARC dissidents killed five alleged members, according to the President. Local media count it as the government's 11th bombing.

colombia|2026-11-22|la jagua de ibirico.text: 22 Nov — La Jagua de Ibirico, Cesar: An attack on an army battalion using improvised ramps to launch explosive devices killed one soldier and wounded 12. The army called it terrorism; both the ELN and the Clan del Golfo operate in the area, and no group has been officially identified.

colombia|2026-11-25|padilla cauca|armed-.text: 25 Nov — Padilla, Cauca: Gunmen ambushed a police patrol escorting municipal officials to a park inauguration, killing patrolmen Kevin David Torres Berdugo and Bairon Jesus Riascos Murillo and wounding four. The Padilla police station was then harassed with gunfire. Some outlets blame FARC dissidents; responsibility has not been officially established.

haiti|2026-11-19|martissant port au prin.text: 19–20 Nov — Martissant, Port-au-Prince: Haitian police units (SWAT, UTAG, UDMO), backed by the Task Force run by private contractor Vectus Global, armoured vehicles and explosive-laden drones, say they killed 54 suspected members of the Village de Dieu and Grand Ravine gangs (34 on 19 November, 20 on 20 November). The aim is to reopen National Road 2 to the south; police reported no losses and did not say what ground was retaken.

haiti|2026-11-20|salvadoran base haiti|o.text: 20 Nov — Salvadoran base, Haiti: An accidental explosion during an operation killed three Salvadoran soldiers, Lt Cristian Daniel Palacios Santos and Corporals Emerson Zepeda Zelada and Wilber Serrano Medina, and injured a fourth. Bukele said the corporals were trying to dislodge a grenade from a drone. He announced a $1 million fund for the families and said troops who want to leave Haiti may do so without reprisal.

haiti|2026-11-22|marassa bridge tabarre.place: Marassa Bridge, Tabarre and Gros-Morne, Artibonite
haiti|2026-11-22|marassa bridge tabarre.text: 22 Nov — Marassa Bridge, Tabarre and Gros-Morne, Artibonite: The GSF said its troops killed six suspected gang members and seized five firearms at the Marassa Bridge. It also killed one in Boston (Cite Soleil) and met armed resistance in Gros-Morne, where a magistrate reported three bodies of suspected Kokorat San Ras members.

haiti|2026-11-25|bongars kenscoff|armed-.text: 25 Nov — Bongars, Kenscoff: Around 04:00, armed men from the Clemenceau area attacked an informal market with firearms and machetes, killing at least 10 farmers and wounding seven (Le Nouvelliste via EFE). Police launched a helicopter-supported pursuit.

cuba|2026-11-21|nationwide|humanitarian.text: 21–23 Nov — Nationwide: The Electric Union (UNE) reported outages lasting all day on 21 November and into the early hours of 22 November. It forecast cuts of 1,713 MW at peak on 22 November and 1,725 MW on 23 November, with only about 1,105 MW available against 2,800 MW of demand.

cuba|2026-11-25|havana|political.text: 25 Nov — Havana: The Independent Trade Union Association of Cuba (ASIC) reported that State Security detained independent unionist Emilio Gottardi Gottardi as he left his home; his whereabouts were unknown.

cuba|2026-11-22|el cobre santiago de cub.text: 22 Nov — El Cobre, Santiago de Cuba: Food-aid organiser Yoel Alejandro Perez Serrano reached 15 days in detention without charges, according to former political prisoner Jose Daniel Ferrer; his arrest had triggered street protests in El Cobre. The Cuban Observatory of Human Rights recorded 3,438 repressive actions from January to October 2026.

ecuador|2026-11-22|guayaquil|armed-attac.text: 22 Nov — Guayaquil (Abel Castillo and Modesto Chavez Franco, south-west): Gunmen opened fire on a family party in the street at about 19:15, killing four people, reportedly with no criminal records, and wounding three. Police gave no motive.

ecuador|2026-11-24|quito washington|dipl.text: 24–25 Nov — Quito/Washington: The New York Times reported that the Trump administration had paused joint military operations with Ecuador by mid-October while investigating possible abuses in a 23 September Ecuadorian raid that killed gang figure Carlos German Munoz Jara. Interior Minister Reimberg said on 25 November that a joint work plan remains and that US aircraft and helicopters are still in the country.

ecuador|ongoing|nationwide|military-acti.text: Ongoing (to 29 Nov) — Nationwide: Authorities are deploying 57,470 police and 34,768 soldiers to secure the 29 November local elections, under the Decree 532 state of exception in eight provinces. The campaign closed on 26 November, two weeks after Huaquillas mayoral candidate Ronald Farfan and council candidate Cristhian Rugel were killed.

peru|2026-11-19|callao|other.text: 19 Nov — Callao: Dirincri police arrested two 17-year-olds over the 17 November killing of El Mandarino bus driver Jose Miranda Torres in Jicamarca. Police link them to the 'La Nueva Hermandad' gang, investigated for contract killing and extortion; six more adults and minors are named as suspects.

peru|2026-11-25|villa el salvador lima|a.text: 25 Nov — Villa El Salvador (Lima): Two gunmen on a motorcycle intercepted a ride-hailing taxi at the junction of Avenida Separadora Industrial and Avenida Jose Carlos Mariategui, near a Metro Line 1 station, and fired up to ten shots, killing the driver. No arrests were reported. RPP counts 64 urban transport drivers killed in 2026.

bolivia|2026-11-24|national|political.text: 24 Nov — National: The government raised the price of diesel by 14.6%, from Bs 17.95 to Bs 20.57 a litre, the third increase of 2026, as part of phasing out subsidies under an IMF agreement. President Paz said prices must track international levels. Transport unions declared themselves in emergency, and the Cochabamba Civic Committee denounced a 'dieselazo'.

bolivia|2026-11-25|sucre oruro potosi la.text: 25 Nov — Sucre, Oruro, Potosi, La Paz: About 40 road blockades were recorded on the first day of a two-day transport strike. Police used tear gas to clear roads in Sucre and detained at least 16 transport workers in Chuquisaca; a highway was blocked in Oruro and there were partial stoppages in Potosi and La Paz.

bolivia|2026-11-25|la paz|political.text: 25 Nov — La Paz: Miners, teachers and factory workers instructed their members to join a national COB march against the diesel hike called for Friday 27 November. Oruro heavy-transport operators proposed an indefinite national strike.

dominican republic|2026-11-23|dajabon el.text: 23 Nov — Dajabon, Elias Pina, Jimani, Pedernales: The Migration Directorate (DGM), supported by the armed forces and police, reported 1,298 detentions and 1,317 deportations to Haiti in one day, with Dajabon recording the most detentions (286). The pace of about 10,000 deportations a week since early November continues.

dominican republic|2026-11-23|santo domi.text: 23 Nov — Santo Domingo: The Duartian Institute warned about the Haitian crisis and called for reinforced border surveillance and continued deportations through Christmas. The government maintains the frontier is calm despite gang tension in Haiti.

jamaica|2026-11-23|knockpatrick manchest.text: 23 Nov — Knockpatrick, Manchester: The mother of Kymani Bindloss, shot dead by police on 2 November in what police called a confrontation, publicly disputed the police account of her son as a murder suspect. An alleged eyewitness says he raised his hands before being shot. The Gleaner says at least 256 people have been killed by the security forces this year.

jamaica|2026-11-24|sligoville st catheri.text: 24 Nov — Sligoville, St Catherine: Ayasus Lawrence, 26, shot nine times during a police-military operation the previous week, was charged with possession of a prohibited weapon, unauthorised possession of ammunition and larceny. His father says he was shot in the back while fleeing.
